original_abstract: Waveguide Quantum Electrodynamics (WQED) offers a suitable stage for controlling the interaction of light with atoms, allowing for collective phenomena such as super- and subradiance. In a chiral waveguide setup, the quantum state evolves through all the Hilbert space, rendering an exact theoretical treatment exponentially hard and unobtained to date for more than $\sim 20$ atoms. In this work, we use a computationally efficient higher order mean-field approximation to model the radiation dynamics in a chirally coupled array of atoms, showing good agreement with recent experimental results. Further, based on a perturbative approximation of the full dynamics, we develop an analytical solution that captures photon statistics for a moderate atom number, $N$, and a homogeneous atom-waveguide coupling, $β$. Finally, we show that capturing the onset of second-order coherence from a fully inverted state requires a fourth-order mean-field approximation, as lower-order treatments fail to account for the necessary four-body correlations. These results illustrate the complex behavior of a symmetry-lacking system, and the methods discussed here provide systematic analytical solutions to which semi-classical methods such as the cumulant expansion or the truncated Wigner approximation can be benchmarked.

title: High Purity OAM Entangled Photons from SPDC with Reduced Spatial Spectral Correlations

original_abstract: Entanglement generated by Spontaneous Parametric Down Conversion (SPDC) involves multiple, often mutually correlated degrees of freedom. title: How to improve the accuracy of semiclassical and quasiclassical dynamics with and without generalized quantum master equations

original_abstract: Semi- and quasi-classical (SC) theories can handle arbitrary interatomic interactions and are thus well-suited to predict quantum dynamics in condensed phases that encode energy and charge transport, spectroscopic responses, and chemical reactivity. However, SC theories can be computationally expensive and inaccurate. When combined with generalized quantum master equations (GQMEs), the resulting SC-GQMEs have been observed to enhance the efficiency and accuracy of SC dynamics. Yet, while the mechanism responsible for improved efficiency is clear, the underlying improved accuracy remains elusive. What is worse, SC-GQMEs can yield unphysical dynamics in challenging parameter regimes -- a shortcoming that might be avoided if the mechanism of accuracy improvement were understood. Here, we uncover this mechanism. We leverage short-time analyses to prove that exact, "left-handed" time-derivatives delay the onset of SC inaccuracy, and show that their numerical integration yields dynamics with improved accuracy, even without the GQME. We find, however, that these derivatives are a double-edged sword: while offering greater short-time accuracy, they become unphysical in challenging parameter regimes. Because short-lived memory kernels can leverage short-time accuracy while circumventing long-time instability, we develop a protocol to unambiguously determine the memory kernel cutoff, even in challenging regimes where previous treatments had failed. Our insights into accuracy improvement and kernel cutoff protocol can be expected to apply to complex systems that go beyond simple models.

title: A Comparative Study of the Streaming Instability: Unstratified Models with Marginally Coupled Grains

original_abstract: The streaming instability is a leading mechanism for concentrating solids and initiating planetesimal formation in protoplanetary disks. Although numerous studies have explored its linear growth, nonlinear evolution, and implications for planet formation, the diversity of numerical methods and dust treatments used across the literature has made it difficult to assess which features of the instability are physically robust and which arise from code-dependent choices. We present the first systematic comparison of seven hydrodynamic codes--spanning finite-volume and finite-difference schemes and modeling dust either as Lagrangian particles or as a pressureless fluid--applied to the unstratified streaming instability with a dimensionless stopping time of unity. All codes reproduce the characteristic sequence of exponential growth, filament formation, and turbulent saturation, demonstrating broad agreement in the qualitative behavior of the instability. Quantitatively, however, the dust model remains the dominant source of variation at moderate resolution: particle-based simulations reach higher peak densities and exhibit broader high-density tails than fluid-based models at $512^2$ resolution, although increasing the number of particles brings their initial maximum density evolution into close agreement with that of dust-fluid models. At $1024^2$, these differences diminish substantially, indicating better agreement of the saturated-state statistics across dust treatments. In terms of computational performance, most particle implementations suffer from imbalanced parallelized loads, while execution on a GPU is at least two to three times more energy efficient and scales better at higher resolutions than on CPUs. title: Projected Hessian Learning: Fast Curvature Supervision for Accurate Machine-Learning Interatomic Potentials
generated_summary:

Instead of supervising all second-derivative elements, PHL uses stochastic Hessian-vector products computed with Hutchinson-type random Gaussian probing vectors, providing unbiased curvature estimates at a fraction of the cost.

The authors compare four training strategies—energy-force (E-F), one-column Hessian-vector product, PHL, and full Hessian supervision—using a chemically diverse dataset spanning reactants, products, transition states, intrinsic reaction coordinates, and normal-mode-sampled geometries. All models share the same architecture, isolating the effect of derivative supervision.

Key results demonstrate that PHL achieves approximately 29% reduction in energy RMSE, 48% in force RMSE, and 77% in Hessian RMSE on extrapolative geometries compared to energy-force training, closely approaching full Hessian training accuracy. Critically, PHL provides over 24-fold speedups relative to full Hessian training, requiring less than 8% of its computational cost. Under data-limited fixed-vector conditions, Hutchinson-based PHL consistently outperforms one-column probing with statistically significant improvements.

These findings establish PHL as a scalable alternative to full Hessian supervision, enabling accurate curvature-informed MLIP training applicable to reactive chemistry and, prospectively, to larger condensed-phase systems where explicit Hessian construction is impractical.
original_abstract: The Hessian matrix (second derivatives) encodes far richer local curvature of the potential energy surface than energies and forces alone. However, training machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) with full Hessians is often impractical because explicitly forming and storing Hessian matrices scales quadratically in cost and memory.   We introduce Projected Hessian Learning (PHL), a scalable second-order training framework that injects curvature information using only Hessian-vector products (HVPs). Rather than constructing the Hessian, PHL projects curvature along stochastic probe directions and uses an unbiased stochastic trace-based loss with favorable system-size scaling, enabling curvature-informed training without quadratic memory growth.   We benchmark PHL on a chemically diverse dataset of reactants, products, transition states, intrinsic reaction coordinates, and normal-mode sampled geometries computed at omegaB97XD/6-31G(d). We compare energy-force training (E-F), two HVP-based schemes (E-F-HVP with one-hot or randomized probes), and full energy-force-Hessian training (E-F-H). With randomized probes per minibatch, both HVP schemes match full-Hessian training in energy, force, and Hessian accuracy while delivering >24x epoch speedups for the small molecular systems studied. In a fixed-probe regime with one HVP per molecule, randomized projections consistently outperform one-column probing, especially for far-from-equilibrium geometries.   Overall, PHL replaces explicit Hessian supervision with force-complexity curvature training, retaining most second-order accuracy gains while scaling to larger, more complex molecular systems.

title: Fundamental Limits on Polarization Entanglement Distribution in Optical Fiber

For the special case where the model reduces to an erasure-dephasing channel, these bounds yield exact formulas for the two-way assisted capacities. The framework is then extended to incorporate dark counts in the detection system.

The key findings reveal two distinct operational regimes for polarization entanglement distribution in optical fiber. In the depolarizing-dominated regime, achievable distances are severely limited. However, when active polarization control is employed, the system enters a dephasing-dominated regime where significantly longer distribution distances become feasible at high rates. The significance of this work lies in providing a comprehensive information-theoretic framework that quantifies ultimate distance and rate limitations for repeaterless polarization entanglement distribution in optical fiber, thereby clarifying the boundaries at which quantum repeaters become necessary. While erasure and Pauli channels have been individually well-studied, their combined analysis in this physically motivated form addresses an important gap in quantum communication theory.
original_abstract: Characterizing the ultimate rates of entanglement distribution is essential for both foundational research and the practical deployment of quantum technologies. To investigate these limits, we introduce an erasure-Pauli channel model describing the distribution of polarization entanglement in optical fiber. For this channel, we derive bounds on the rates of entanglement distribution and related quantum resources under optimal local operations and two-way classical communication (two-way assisted capacities). This framework allows us to determine the optimal repeaterless performance achievable over realistic optical fibers affected by polarization mode dispersion, thereby providing a rigorous benchmark for long-distance polarization-based quantum communication. Finally, we show that both our model and capacity bounds remain robust under the inclusion of detector dark counts.

title: Accurate and Efficient Hybrid-Ensemble Atmospheric Data Assimilation in Latent Space with Uncertainty Quantification

Critically, it requires only approximately 3% of the runtime and 20% of the memory of variational alternatives. original_abstract: Data assimilation (DA) combines model forecasts and observations to estimate the optimal state of the atmosphere with its uncertainty, providing initial conditions for weather prediction and reanalyses for climate research. Yet, existing traditional and machine-learning DA methods struggle to achieve accuracy, efficiency and uncertainty quantification simultaneously. Here, we propose HLOBA (Hybrid-Ensemble Latent Observation-Background Assimilation), a three-dimensional hybrid-ensemble DA method that operates in an atmospheric latent space learned via an autoencoder (AE). HLOBA maps both model forecasts and observations into a shared latent space via the AE encoder and an end-to-end Observation-to-Latent-space mapping network (O2Lnet), respectively, and fuses them through a Bayesian update with weights inferred from time-lagged ensemble forecasts. Both idealized and real-observation experiments demonstrate that HLOBA matches dynamically constrained four-dimensional DA methods in both analysis and forecast skill, while achieving end-to-end inference-level efficiency and theoretical flexibility applies to any forecasting model. Moreover, by exploiting the error decorrelation property of latent variables, HLOBA enables element-wise uncertainty estimates for its latent analysis and propagates them to model space via the decoder. Idealized experiments show that this uncertainty highlights large-error regions and captures their seasonal variability.

title: Hyperuniform Disorder in Photonic Crystal Slabs with Intrinsic non-Hermiticity

The authors develop an analytical framework based on self-energy calculations and spectral function analysis to quantify scattering losses introduced by hyperuniform disorder—a special class of correlated disorder characterized by suppressed long-wavelength density fluctuations, parameterized by a hyperuniformity exponent α. For Hermitian systems with quadratic bands, they show that the excess linewidth due to scattering scales as a power law proportional to the disorder strength squared times momentum raised to 2α + d − 2, where d is the spatial dimension. However, in the non-Hermitian case with complex effective mass, the scaling behavior changes dramatically: when α exceeds a critical threshold, the leading-order excess linewidth becomes proportional to the disorder strength squared multiplied by a finite constant, with the next-order correction never exceeding a specific exponent dependent on α.

original_abstract: Hyperuniform disorder is a type of correlated disorder characterized by vanishing spectral density at small wavevectors, making the configuration effectively homogeneous on long length scales. In photonics, hyperuniform disorder is promising for generating isotropic photonic pseudogaps and engineering photonic crystal waveguides. However, these studies are largely restricted to idealized lossless settings, although all photonic systems necessarily have loss. In this work, light propagation in photonic crystal slabs with imposed hyperuniform disorder is investigated theoretically and numerically. The system is intrinsically non-Hermitian due to radiative loss, with non-Hermiticity appearing as a complex effective mass of a quadratic photonic band. A theoretical framework for disorder scattering is analytically derived in Hermitian and non-Hermitian quadratic bands with real and complex effective mass, respectively. In contrast to the power law behavior $|\mathbf{k}|^α$ observed in the Hermitian case (where $α$ is the hyperuniformity exponent), the scattering loss in the non-Hermitian band is given by $C_0+C_{β_2}\cdot|\mathbf{k}|^{β_2}$, where $C_0$ is a finite constant and the exponent $β_2\leq 2$. Our theoretical predictions are verified with tight-binding and Finite-Difference Time-Domain simulations with realistic photonic crystal parameters, based on recent experiments.

title: Dynamic properties in a collisional model for confined granular fluids. A review

This review examines the Δ-model, a collisional framework developed to describe the dynamics of confined quasi-two-dimensional granular fluids. The parameter Δ represents a fixed velocity increment along the collision normal direction, capturing the effective transfer of kinetic energy from vertical to horizontal degrees of freedom that occurs in vibrated shallow granular systems.

The methodology employs Enskog kinetic theory combined with Chapman-Enskog expansions to derive Navier-Stokes hydrodynamic equations and explicit transport coefficients—including shear viscosity, thermal conductivity, and diffusive heat conductivity—for both monocomponent systems and binary mixtures. Theoretical predictions are validated against molecular dynamics simulations and direct simulation Monte Carlo methods.

Key results demonstrate that the Δ-model produces stable, spatially homogeneous non-equilibrium steady states where energy dissipation and injection balance globally. The model naturally exhibits breakdown of energy equipartition in mixtures, with each species reaching different granular temperatures. Transport coefficients show nontrivial dependence on the coefficient of restitution and volume fraction, with good agreement between theory and simulations.

The significance of this work lies in providing a tractable kinetic theory framework that connects microscopic collision mechanisms to macroscopic transport properties, while also capturing complex phenomena including Brazil nut effects, quasicrystal formation, and hyperuniformity in granular systems.
original_abstract: Granular systems confined in a shallow box and driven by vertical vibration provide a simple geometry to study fluidized granular media. Grains gain kinetic energy vertically through collisions with the walls and redistribute it horizontally via interparticle collisions. The $Δ$-model has been proposed as a simplified description of this setup. In this model, a fixed velocity increment $Δ$ is added to the normal component of the relative velocity at collisions, effectively integrating out the vertical motion while preserving collisional energy injection. This compensates for inelastic losses and yields stable homogeneous steady states amenable to kinetic theory. An Enskog kinetic equation is formulated and analyzed to obtain the stationary temperature and equation of state. The Chapman--Enskog method is then applied to derive the Navier--Stokes transport coefficients and study inhomogeneous states. The theory is extended to granular mixtures with different masses, sizes, restitution coefficients, or $Δ$ values, leading to nonequipartition of energy even in homogeneous states. The resulting hydrodynamic equations, with transport coefficients obtained in the low-density regime, show unconditional stability of the homogeneous state and violation of Onsager reciprocity. Theoretical predictions agree well with molecular dynamics and direct simulation Monte Carlo results.

title: Coherent Biexciton Transport in the Presence of Exciton-Exciton Annihilation in Molecular Aggregates

original_abstract: We present a theoretical framework for biexciton dynamics in molecular aggregates that explicitly treats populations and coherences across excitation manifolds within a reduced density-matrix formalism. title: The self-generation of core fields and electron scattering in flux ropes during magnetic reconnection

title: Optomicrofluidic measurement of particle-encapsulated droplet system

title: A Multi-Fidelity Parametric Framework for Reduced-Order Modeling using Optimal Transport-based Interpolation: Applications to Diffused-Interface Two-Phase Flows

title: False Metallization in Short-Ranged Machine Learned Interatomic Potentials

title: Graphs are focal hypergraphs: strict containment in higher-order interaction dynamics

Closed graph neighbourhoods are precisely focal hyperedges, so hyperedges generalise graph neighbourhoods by removing the focal constraint. This yields a strict three-level hierarchy: graph models $\subsetneq$ focal hypergraph models $\subsetneq$ general hypergraph models. Moreover, graph models do encode genuinely higher-order (many-body) interactions, in the sense that each node's update function may depend jointly on all members of its closed neighbourhood, but they remain a strict special case of the hypergraph dynamical model, not equivalent to it. We further show that universal encodings such as bipartite factor graphs are neutral with respect to this hierarchy, and that the symmetry condition of the hypergraph dynamical model -- often treated as an additional constraint relative to the graph model -- is in fact the dynamical definition of a non-focal interaction. The taxonomy is grounded in concrete phenomena from physics, biology, ecology, and social systems, and yields a principle of representational alignment: the choice between graph and hypergraph models should be governed by the type of interaction, not by a blanket preference for one formalism over the other.

title: Cell-Cell Adhesion as a Double-Edged Sword in Tissue Fluidity
generated_summary:
This study resolves a longstanding paradox regarding cell-cell adhesion's role in tissue fluidity by extending the classical vertex model to explicitly distinguish two mechanistically distinct contributions of adhesion: an energetic component that reduces junctional tension and a kinetic (dissipative) component that resists relative cell motion. The kinetic component is derived from a microscopic model of receptor-ligand binding kinetics, which produces an effective viscous drag force proportional to relative cell velocity at shared interfaces.

The authors systematically investigate tissue dynamics across both adhesion parameters using mean squared displacement, self-intermediate scattering functions, and effective diffusivity as order parameters. They construct a phase diagram revealing that increasing energetic adhesion promotes tissue fluidization by facilitating cell rearrangements, while increasing kinetic adhesion drives jamming by penalizing changes in junction geometry. This non-monotonic dependence on total adhesion strength reconciles previously contradictory experimental observations.

Rheological analysis under oscillatory and step-strain deformation reveals that modeled tissues exhibit power-law viscoelastic behavior rather than simple exponential relaxation, well-captured by fractional viscoelastic models. This indicates an intrinsic broad spectrum of relaxation times. The framework is validated against MDCK monolayer experiments showing shape-independent fluidity changes and Drosophila embryo morphogenetic flows.

This work establishes that dissipative adhesion is a central, previously underappreciated regulator of epithelial tissue mechanics, challenging the prevailing geometric paradigm where cell shape alone governs rigidity transitions.
original_abstract: Cell migration plays a fundamental role in numerous physiological processes, including embryonic development, wound healing, and cancer metastasis. While cell-cell adhesion is known to regulate motion by shaping cell morphology and intercellular force balance, its dynamic, rate-dependent contributions to tissue behavior remain poorly understood. In this study, we examine how the dissipative nature of cell-cell adhesion influences tissue dynamics and collective migration using an extended vertex model with explicit junctional viscosity. Our findings reveal a nontrivial interplay between two distinct components of adhesion: an interfacial adhesion energy (energetic, rate-independent) contribution, which sets the effective junctional tension, and a dissipative (rate-dependent) contribution, which controls resistance to relative motion during cell rearrangements. We show that increasing the energetic component promotes migration by modifying cell shape and lowering the barrier to neighbor exchanges, whereas strengthening the dissipative component induces jamming and suppresses cell motion. Linear rheological analysis further demonstrates that, in the unjammed regime, vertex-model tissues exhibit power-law viscoelastic behavior, with adhesion modulating the power-law exponent and thereby controlling the spread of relaxation timescales. Together, these findings clarify the dual role of adhesion in governing tissue mechanics and rheology and provide a mechanistic framework for understanding the balance between fluidity and rigidity in epithelial monolayers.

title: Observational Indistinguishability and the Beginning of the Universe
generated_summary:
This paper investigates whether we can observationally establish that all of physical reality had a beginning, arguing that we cannot. The main contribution is a series of new theorems demonstrating that spacetimes satisfying conditions intuitively required for a cosmic beginning are observationally indistinguishable from spacetimes that lack such a beginning.

The author builds on the Malament-Manchak framework, which establishes fundamental limits on our ability to determine the global structure of spacetime from local observations. The methodology involves proving corollaries to the Malament-Manchak theorem using geometric constructions (including "clothesline" constructions) that produce observationally indistinguishable counterpart spacetimes. The paper also introduces mathematical techniques from astrophysical applications not previously connected to this philosophical debate.

Key results show that spacetimes satisfying global conditions required by the classic singularity theorems have observationally indistinguishable counterparts that fail to satisfy those conditions; spacetimes with temporal ordering intuitively needed for a beginning are indistinguishable from those without it; and spacetimes with singularities to the past of every point are indistinguishable from those lacking this property. Notably, all dust-filled FLRW spacetimes with past singularities possess counterparts sharing many physical properties yet lacking universal past singularities. The paper also argues that strategies relying on rejecting individual cosmological models as implausible commit an error in confirmation theory.

These results have profound implications for cosmological epistemology, suggesting that observational evidence alone cannot establish whether all of spacetime had a common origin.
original_abstract: Can we infer whether all of physical reality began to exist? Several novel results are offered suggesting a negative verdict. First, a common strategy for defending a cosmic beginning involves showing that individual beginningless cosmological models are implausible. This strategy is shown to make an elementary error in confirmation theory. Second, two necessary (but not necessarily sufficient) conditions are offered for a cosmic beginning. Third, three extensions are offered to the Malament-Manchak theorems. The three extensions show that in almost all classical spacetimes, observers cannot collect sufficient data to determine whether the application conditions for the classic singularity theorems are satisfied or whether their spacetime satisfies the two necessary conditions for a cosmic beginning. Lastly, a reply is offered to the objection that the skeptical consequences of the three extensions can be overcome with induction. Importantly, all past singular dust FLRW spacetimes have observationally indistinguishable counterparts which, while sharing a number of important local properties, either do not include a singularity to the past of every point or else do not have the sort of time ordering intuitively required for a cosmic beginning.

title: Structure-resolved free energy estimation of the 38-atom Lennard Jones cluster via population annealing
generated_summary:
This study demonstrates the application of population annealing (PA), a sequential Monte Carlo method, to obtain structure-resolved free energy estimates for the 38-atom Lennard-Jones cluster (LJ₃₈), a notoriously challenging benchmark system featuring a double-funnel energy landscape with competing face-centered cubic (FCC) and icosahedral structural motifs.

The methodology combines PA with an adaptive temperature schedule, configuration quenching to local energy minima via the FIRE minimization algorithm, and subsequent structural classification using principal component analysis of bond-orientational order parameters followed by k-means clustering. This workflow enables the decomposition of the total free energy into contributions from distinct structural basins—FCC-like, icosahedral, and liquid-like—without relying on harmonic approximations. The PA reweighting framework provides direct free energy estimates at each temperature step, while the large population of walkers maintains ensemble diversity across high free energy barriers.

Key results confirm the convergence of thermodynamic observables with increasing population size and reveal the temperature-dependent competition among the three structural families. The free energy analysis quantitatively captures the solid-solid crossover between FCC and icosahedral basins and their relative stability as a function of temperature, consistent with known thermodynamic behavior of LJ₃₈.

The significance of this work lies in establishing a practical, scalable framework for mapping finite-temperature free energy landscapes in molecular systems with competing structural motifs, leveraging PA's inherent suitability for massively parallel architectures and its capacity for direct free energy estimation.
original_abstract: We systematically investigate the thermodynamic landscape of the 38-atom Lennard--Jones cluster LJ$_{38}$ using Population Annealing (PA), a method suited for systems with challenging double-funnel energy landscapes. By employing an adaptive temperature schedule, we demonstrate that thermodynamic observables, such as internal energy and heat capacity, converge robustly when the population size is sufficiently large. To gain deeper insights into the competing basins, we introduce an integrated framework that combines PA reweighting factors with structure-resolved analysis. Using quenched configurations characterized by potential energy and Steinhardt's bond-orientational order parameters, we identify three structural basins, FCC-like, icosahedral, and liquid-like, via dimensionality reduction and clustering. This framework enables the direct computation of structure-resolved free energy differences from population fractions, providing a quantitative mapping of the thermodynamic competition between the funnels. The resulting structural crossovers are consistent with the heat-capacity peak, demonstrating PA as a promising and scalable framework for structure-resolved thermodynamics in complex molecular systems.

title: Machine-learned Interatomic Potential for Ti$_{n+1}$C$_n$ MXenes: Application to Ion Irradiation Simulations
generated_summary:
This study presents a machine-learned interatomic potential for Ti_{n+1}C_n MXenes using the tabulated Gaussian approximation potential (tabGAP) framework, addressing the critical lack of reliable interatomic potentials for molecular dynamics simulations of these promising 2D materials. The potential is trained on a diverse database of DFT-calculated structures encompassing MXenes of varying thicknesses and stackings, non-MXene reference structures, and iteratively learned configurations. A pre-fitted Ziegler-Biersack-Littmark repulsive potential is incorporated to enable accurate simulation of high-energy atomic collisions.

The potential's accuracy is validated against DFT for elastic properties, lattice constants, vacancy formation energies, phonon dispersions, plastic shear response, and quasi-static sputtering drag calculations, demonstrating excellent agreement across all benchmarks. The potential is then applied to simulate He and Ti ion irradiation of Ti₂C and Ti₃C₂ MXene sheets across energies spanning four orders of magnitude (15 eV to 100 keV), with 10,000 independent impacts per energy for statistical reliability.

Key findings include quantification of ion reflection, implantation, and pass-through probabilities as functions of energy, confirmation of preferential Ti sputtering at higher energies, and the discovery that C sputtering onset occurs at lower energies for light-ion irradiation. Notably, the simulations reveal remarkable structural resilience of MXene sheets, with heavily damaged regions efficiently recrystallizing and healing. This work establishes a transferable framework for developing ML potentials for the broader MXene family, enabling computational guidance for defect engineering through ion irradiation.
original_abstract: A computationally efficient and accurate machine-learned (ML) interatomic potential is developed for Ti$_{n+1}$C$_n$ MXenes. With a diverse set of structures computed with density functional theory, the trained ML potential demonstrates good accuracy and robustness to a wide range of bond distances and environments, making it a useful tool for molecular dynamics simulations of MXenes subjected to mechanical load or irradiation. The ML potential is applied to simulations of light and heavy ion irradiation, gathering insight into the statistics and probabilities of sputtering, reflection, defect creation, and implantation into Ti$_{n+1}$C$_n$ MXene sheets. The results provide guidelines for defect engineering of MXenes through ion irradiation and implantation. Additionally, the ML potential development provides a landmark recipe for enabling machine-learning-driven atomistic simulations of other MXenes.

title: Nine-element machine-learned interatomic potentials for multiphase refractory alloys
generated_summary:
This paper presents the development of a comprehensive database (RHEA) and two machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs)—tabGAP and NEP—for nine refractory elements (Ti, Zr, Hf, V, Nb, Ta, Cr, Mo, W) and their arbitrary alloys. The work fills an important gap between limited single-element MLIPs and computationally expensive universal foundation potentials, targeting the vast compositional space relevant to refractory high-entropy alloys.

The RHEA database was constructed through systematic sampling of binary through nine-element alloys across multiple crystal structures, liquid phases, intermetallic compounds, and defect configurations. A novel cross-sampling active learning strategy was employed, leveraging disagreements between the two architecturally distinct MLIPs to identify structures requiring additional training data, complementing traditional active learning approaches.

Both MLIPs accurately reproduce fundamental materials properties including equations of state, formation energies, bulk moduli, defect energies, and melting points across all nine elements. The potentials successfully predict pressure-temperature phase diagrams of Ti, Zr, and Hf, composition-dependent phase transitions in Zr-Nb alloys consistent with experimental phase diagrams, and grain boundary segregation trends matching experimental observations in four different refractory alloys. Large-scale simulations of radiation damage in a million-atom W₂₄Ta₂₄Cr₂₄V₂₄Hf₄ metallic glass demonstrate the glass's radiation resistance, consistent with experimental findings.

These computationally efficient MLIPs enable multimillion-atom simulations of refractory alloys under both equilibrium and extreme conditions, providing valuable tools for high-entropy alloy design and understanding.
original_abstract: New refractory alloys are being continuously designed and characterised for applications requiring good high-temperature mechanical properties and stability. Computational design from atomistic simulations is limited by interatomic potentials missing key elements, being too inaccurate, or computationally too slow for large-scale simulations. Here we present development of a refractory alloy database and two computationally efficient and general-purpose machine-learned potentials (tabGAP and NEP). We also design a cross-sampling strategy for effective sampling of training data using predictions from two potentials with completely different underlying architecture. The potentials support arbitrary alloy compositions of elements in groups four to six in the periodic table (Ti, Zr, Hf, V, Nb, Ta, Cr, Mo, W). The database is diverse yet multitargeted to enable simulations of refractory metals and alloys across different pure-metal, solid-solution, intermetallic, and glassy phases. We demonstrate the usefulness of the potentials by reproducing known pressure-, temperature-, and solute-induced phase transitions, grain boundary segregation, and simulations of radiation damage in the WTaCrVHf metallic glass.

title: Atomic-scale Stark-shift spectroscopy and microscopy of organic molecules
generated_summary:
This paper presents a theoretical framework for atomic-scale Stark-shift spectroscopy and microscopy of organic molecules using scanning tunneling microscope-induced luminescence (STML). The key contribution is a perturbative treatment that systematically separates linear and quadratic Stark-shift contributions when molecules are subjected to strongly inhomogeneous electrostatic fields generated by an atomically sharp STM tip.

The methodology employs time-dependent density functional theory (TD-DFT) calculations using the B3LYP functional and 6-31G* basis set. External point charges mimicking the STM tip are systematically positioned over molecular planes, and the resulting changes in excitation energies are decomposed into linear and quadratic components through analysis of ground-state and excited-state charge density differences and induced charge densities.

The authors analyze several molecular families, including phthalocyanines, acenes, quinacridone, and rylene derivatives. A central finding is that inhomogeneous fields produce strong linear Stark shifts even in centrosymmetric molecules, representing a breakdown of the dipolar selection rules that govern conventional homogeneous-field Stark spectroscopy. The spatially resolved Stark-shift maps directly reflect intramolecular charge redistribution upon excitation, and small chemical modifications—such as adding functional groups—substantially alter the Stark-shift response.

The significance of this work lies in establishing atomic-scale Stark-shift microscopy as a potential tool for imaging charge transfer processes in molecular systems, assessing emission stability near defects, and advancing the development of robust single-photon emitters.
original_abstract: In conventional optical Stark-shift spectroscopy, molecules are exposed to spatially homogeneous static electric fields that shift the energies of their spectral lines. These shifts are attributed to the molecular electronic properties, such as variation of dipolar moment and polarizability of the molecule associated with photo(de)excitation. In realistic environments containing structural defects and nanoscale heterogeneities, however, molecules experience internal electric fields that vary strongly on the molecular scale, rendering the standard Stark selection rules inapplicable. Here we develop an extended theory of atomic-scale Stark shift, addressing such scenarios. Specifically, we present a detailed theoretical analysis of an experimentally relevant configuration where the atomically sharp tip of a light-assisted scanning tunneling microscope is used to controllably apply inhomogeneous electrostatic fields to representative molecular dyes spanning several molecular families. We decompose the total Stark shift into linear and quadratic contributions and show that they contain different information about the molecular properties. Concretely, spatial variations of the linear Stark shift as the tip scans across the molecule enable subnanometric mapping of the charge redistribution between ground and excited electronic states, with high sensitivity to molecular composition and chemical functionalization. The quadratic Stark contribution, in contrast, reflects changes in the conventional dipolar polarizability upon excitation. Together, these results establish nanoscale Stark-shift spectroscopy as a powerful tool for resolving excited-state charge dynamics in single molecules under realistic, strongly inhomogeneous electric fields.

title: Evaluation of the performance of an analytical-numerical coupled method for droplet impacts on soft material surfaces
generated_summary:
This study evaluates the applicability limits of an analytical-numerical coupled method (ANCM) for simulating liquid droplet impacts on soft material surfaces. The ANCM, previously developed for stiff materials, replaces computationally expensive fluid dynamics simulations with an analytical pressure solution derived for rigid surfaces, applying it as a boundary condition in finite element (FE) analysis. The key question is whether this rigid-surface assumption remains valid for compliant soft materials.

The authors compare the ANCM against a conventional Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics (SPH) model and experimental data from silicone oil droplet impacts on urethane gel, conducting a parametric study across five Young's modulus values ranging from 500 Pa to 500 kPa. The ANCM achieves results in approximately 12 minutes compared to 1540 minutes for SPH at equivalent computational resources.

Results show the ANCM agrees well with SPH and experimental data for materials with Young's modulus of 50 kPa or stiffer. Below this threshold, discrepancies emerge because the ANCM applies pressure independent of surface deformation, while SPH correctly redirects impact loads normal to the deforming surface. A fundamental breakdown occurs at approximately 5 kPa (gelatine-like softness), where the ANCM produces non-physical overshoots in impact force and surface displacement, including steep wall craters. The authors identify 50 kPa as the onset of the ANCM failure zone, establishing a practical applicability limit. These findings guide engineers in selecting appropriate modeling approaches for soft material impact problems across biomedical and industrial applications.
original_abstract: Impacts between droplets and solid surfaces can commonly cause erosion problem in Engineering applications, including aircraft surface erosion, wind blade leading-edge erosion and steam turbine blade erosion. In practice, the impacted solid surfaces have varied material softness, ranging from stiff metallic coatings to soft materials. An analytical-numerical coupled model (ANCM) for simulating droplet impacts on surfaces, and corresponding material analysis, has been developed in the literature. However, the analytical impact pressure solution of the ANCM model has been derived assuming rigid solid surface. In the current study, we investigate the performance of the ANCM model for droplet impacts on soft materials made of urethane gel phantom, by comparing the ANCM computations to lab-based experiments and numerical simulations based on Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics (SPH). Parametric studies explore the applicability limit of the ANCM model for droplet impacts on very soft materials at low Young's modulus. It was found that for materials at Young's modulus of $47,400$ Pa or stiffer, which covers most engineering applications, the developed ANCM model performs as expected for an assumed rigid surface. For softer solid materials, the SPH-modeled liquid interacts with the evolving surface geometry and mitigates impact intensity as deformation occurs. The analytical impact loads estimated by ANCM are independent of surface geometry, and hence provide conserved impact impulse in a non-physical way. Results show a critical value of Young's modulus at $E=10,000$ pa for the ANCM model, below which the model exhibits overshoot in total contact force and surface deformation, leading to the formation of steep wall craters.

title: Irradiation Studies of TGC Electronics Components for the ATLAS Experiment at High-Luminosity LHC
generated_summary:
This paper presents comprehensive radiation tolerance evaluations of commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) electronic components intended for the Thin Gap Chamber (TGC) frontend electronics upgrade of the ATLAS experiment at the High-Luminosity Large Hadron Collider (HL-LHC). The frontend electronics, located near the detector, must withstand significant radiation exposure over the planned ten-year operational period.

The study evaluates both Total Ionizing Dose (TID) and Non-Ionizing Energy Loss (NIEL) effects on a wide range of components, including SFP+ optical transceivers, clock jitter cleaners, optical fibers, voltage references, operational amplifiers, ADCs, DACs, SD cards, flash memories, and low-dropout regulators. TID testing was performed using a Cobalt-60 gamma-ray source at Nagoya University, while NIEL testing utilized neutron irradiation from the Tandem Accelerator at Kobe University. For each component, the maximum functional dose was determined and compared against requirements that include appropriate safety factors.

All tested components met the radiation tolerance requirements for ten years of HL-LHC operation, including applied safety factors, demonstrating sufficient tolerance to both TID and NIEL effects. Neutron-irradiated components remained operational after exposures on the order of 10¹¹ neutrons per square centimeter. Based on these results, specific component models were selected for full production of the TGC frontend electronics, which was completed and successfully verified through final quality testing on fully assembled boards in 2025. These findings are critical for ensuring reliable muon trigger detector operation throughout the HL-LHC era.
original_abstract: This paper evaluates the radiation tolerance of commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) electronics components for use in the Thin Gap Chamber (TGC) frontend electronics of the ATLAS experiment at the High-Luminosity LHC (HL-LHC). The ATLAS experiment has accumulated more than 450 fb^-1 of data as of 2025. Its luminosity upgrade, the HL-LHC scheduled to begin operation in 2030, will deliver 3000-4000 fb^-1 over ten years and lead to substantially higher radiation levels in detector electronics. The radiation levels for the TGC frontend electronics are estimated to be 4.1-7.3 Gy in terms of Total Ionizing Dose (TID) and 1.1-2.2 x 10^11 n_1MeV cm^-2 in terms of Non-Ionizing Energy Loss (NIEL). To evaluate component suitability under these conditions, TID tests were conducted using Cobalt-60 gamma rays at Nagoya University, and NIEL tests were performed with the Tandem Accelerator at Kobe University. Various COTS components, including SFP+ optical transceivers, clock jitter cleaners, optical fibers, voltage references, operational amplifiers, analog-to-digital converters, digital-to-analog converters, SD cards, flash memories, and low-dropout regulators, were tested and evaluated against the required radiation levels. The results demonstrate that all evaluated components meet the TID and NIEL tolerance requirements for application in the TGC frontend electronics at the HL-LHC.

title: An analytical-numerical coupled model of liquid droplet impact on solid material surfaces
generated_summary:
This study presents an analytical-numerical coupled method (ANCM) for simulating liquid droplet impact on solid surfaces, addressing the high computational cost of conventional fully numerical approaches. The main contribution is twofold: deriving an explicit, closed-form analytical solution for droplet impact pressure throughout the full impact and spreading phases, and coupling this analytical liquid-phase solution with finite element (FE) analysis of the solid response.

The methodology modifies Wagner's theoretical framework by incorporating a separation point concept and extending the analytical pressure solution from early impact through the inertia-driven spreading regime. This analytical pressure loading is applied as a boundary condition on the solid surface in an FE simulation, eliminating the need to explicitly model the liquid phase. The approach is validated against experimental data and conventional smoothed particle hydrodynamics (SPH) simulations of a water droplet impacting an aluminium plate.

Key results show that ANCM produces smooth, oscillation-free pressure, stress, and displacement fields, whereas SPH exhibits pronounced spurious oscillations requiring significant mesh refinement. ANCM achieves grid independence at substantially lower resolutions and requires only a fraction of SPH's computational cost. Both methods capture characteristic ring-shaped pressure patterns on the impact surface consistent with experimentally observed erosion patterns.

The framework offers a computationally efficient and accurate alternative for studying liquid-solid impact erosion in engineering applications, including wind turbine blade leading-edge erosion, steam turbine blade erosion, and aircraft rain erosion.
original_abstract: Impacts of liquid droplets on wind turbine blade surfaces, for example sea sprays, can result in material damage through erosion. In this study, we derive an explicit, closed-form analytical approximation for droplet impact and subsequent spreading on a solid surface in inertia-dominated regimes of large Reynolds and Weber numbers. The formulation extends an existing theoretical framework based on inviscid potential flow for a rising expanding disk in an infinite liquid domain. The modified solution provides full spatio-temporal pressure distributions and impact force histories on the impact surface over the entire impact duration, capturing both the early-time self-similar flow and the inertia-driven lamella spreading following the peak impact force. The predicted pressure and force profiles show good agreement with analytical, numerical and experimental results reported in the literature, including accurate reproduction of the well-known ring-shaped pressure distribution. Key quantities, such as the radial location and magnitude of peak pressure, as well as the timing and magnitude of the peak impact force, are predicted analytically with reasonable accuracy. To enable solid material erosion analysis, the analytical liquid-phase solution is coupled with a finite-element (FE) simulation for the solid response. This analytical-numerical coupled method (ANCM) eliminates the need to explicitly simulate droplet fluid dynamics, which is conventionally performed using smoothed particle hydrodynamics (SPH). As a result, for the purpose of material response analysis, the proposed approach achieves grid independence at substantially lower mesh resolutions and reduces computational cost by more than 97% compared to SPH-based simulations, while maintaining or improving numerical accuracy.

title: The CMS ME0 Upgrade: Enhancing Forward Muon Reconstruction at the HL-LHC
generated_summary:
The paper presents the ME0 detector upgrade for the CMS experiment at the High-Luminosity Large Hadron Collider (HL-LHC), designed to extend forward muon detection coverage to pseudorapidity |η| ≤ 2.8. The ME0 station, based on Gas Electron Multiplier (GEM) technology, will be positioned behind the High-Granularity Calorimeter (HGCal) as the first muon detection layer encountered by tracks from the interaction point. This upgrade addresses the challenges of increased radiation and high particle rates expected at HL-LHC luminosities of approximately 5–7 × 10³⁴ cm⁻² s⁻¹.

The methodology encompasses rigorous quality control during module production, including gas leak measurements that demonstrate exponential pressure decrease behavior consistent with expected models. Performance characterization is conducted at the CERN GIF++ facility under high-rate conditions, as well as through cosmic ray testing to evaluate timing properties.

Key results demonstrate that ME0 modules maintain detection efficiency above 97% as a function of hit rate, confirming stable performance even under the demanding conditions expected at the HL-LHC. Timing resolution measurements from cosmic tests characterize both individual ME0 layers and the full six-layer stack configuration.

The significance of this upgrade lies in its enhancement of CMS forward muon reconstruction capabilities, improving tracking performance, trigger efficiency, and background rejection in the forward region—critical for maintaining physics sensitivity throughout the HL-LHC program.
original_abstract: The CMS muon system is undergoing substantial upgrades to meet the challenges of the High-Luminosity LHC (HL-LHC), including the installation of the new Muon Endcap 0 (ME0) detector. Large-scale production started in 2024. ME0 is a six-layer station designed to extend pseudo-rapidity coverage to |η| = 2.8 from the previous maximum of |η| = 2.4, enhancing sensitivity to forward physics processes. Each endcap will host 18 ME0 stacks, with each stack comprising six triple-layer gas electron multiplier (GEM) chambers. The system adds up to six additional hits per track, which significantly improves muon identification, spatial resolution, and robust track reconstruction at the first trigger level. Chamber production and quality control across multiple international sites ensure scalability and timely delivery. The ME0 design incorporates lessons learned from earlier GEM deployments, with improvements in electronics robustness, grounding, and segmentation to withstand high background rates and minimize damage from discharges. This contribution provides a comprehensive overview of the ME0 detector concept, assembly strategy, quality assurance procedures, current production status, and its pivotal role in strengthening CMS muon reconstruction during HL-LHC operations.

title: Optimally Tuned Multiconfigurational Short-Range DFT for Linear Response Properties
generated_summary:
This paper introduces an optimally tuned multiconfigurational short-range density functional theory (MC-srDFT) approach for computing linear response properties, specifically molecular polarizabilities. The main contribution is a rigorous, physically motivated protocol for determining the range-separation parameter μ within MC-srDFT, based on an exact extension of the Koopmans condition and the requirement that the method reproduces the correct long-range asymptotic decay of the electron density. Previously, MC-srDFT relied on a universal parameter value (typically μ = 0.4 bohr⁻¹), which proved suboptimal for many applications.

The authors assess their optimally tuned approach by computing static and dynamic dipole polarizabilities for a benchmark set of molecules, comparing results against CC3 reference data. They employ both full time-dependent MC-srDFT linear response and the computationally more efficient extended random phase approximation (ERPA), which neglects wavefunction expansion coefficient responses while retaining orbital relaxation contributions. Short-range exchange-correlation effects are treated with a local density approximation functional.

Key results demonstrate that optimal tuning significantly improves polarizability predictions compared to the standard universal μ value, reducing mean absolute errors relative to CC3 benchmarks. The tuned parameter values vary across molecules but cluster within a defined range. The ERPA variant offers favorable computational scaling with active space size while maintaining reasonable accuracy.

This work establishes a systematic parameter-determination framework for MC-srDFT response properties, bridging a methodological gap that previously existed only in single-reference range-separated DFT, with implications for reliable prediction of molecular response properties in multireference systems.
original_abstract: Multiconfigurational short-range density functional theory (MC-srDFT) rigorously combines ground state wavefunction theory with DFT. Unlike single-reference range-separated hybrid functionals, MC-srDFT has lacked theoretically grounded protocols for choosing the system-specific range-separation parameter. To address this problem, we introduce an optimal-tuning scheme based on enforcing the correct exponential decay of the electron density. We show that the range-separation parameter can be determined from the ionization potential given by the smallest-magnitude eigenvalue of the Extended Koopmans' Theorem matrix constructed for the model Hamiltonian. We validate this approach for static and dynamic dipole polarizabilities of ground-state molecular systems using MC-srDFT within both full linear response and its extended random phase approximation (ERPA) variant. Optimal tuning substantially improves polarizabilities relative to the commonly used universal $μ= 0.4\,\mathrm{bohr}^{-1}$ parameter.

title: Reducing hyperparameter sensitivity in measurement-feedback based Ising machines
generated_summary:
This paper investigates the dynamical differences between time-continuous and time-discrete analog Ising machines (IMs), which are physics-inspired devices designed to solve combinatorial optimization problems by minimizing an Ising Hamiltonian. The authors identify a critical practical challenge: hyperparameters optimized through time-continuous simulations fail to produce good solutions when transferred to hybrid opto-electronic hardware, which operates in a time-discrete regime due to digital processing delays in the feedback loop.

Through systematic analysis, the authors derive the mathematical relationship between time-continuous dynamics (modeled by differential equations) and time-discrete dynamics (modeled by iterative maps), showing that the distinction reduces to the choice of an Euler integration step size parameter. They demonstrate through brute-force parameter grid scans that the time-discrete system exhibits a significantly narrower range of useful hyperparameter values compared to the time-continuous case, making it substantially more sensitive to parameter tuning.

To address this limitation, the authors propose introducing a small artificial Euler integration step into the discrete update rule, effectively interpolating between the two dynamical regimes. This approach widens the useful parameter space and reduces sensitivity to hyperparameter initialization and tuning. The method is experimentally validated on an opto-electronic coherent Ising machine using MaxCut benchmark problems from the BiqMac library. Importantly, the proposed solution is hardware-agnostic, as it is independent of the specific nonlinearity used, making it broadly applicable to the many hybrid analog IM implementations currently in development.
original_abstract: Analog Ising machines have been proposed as heuristic hardware solvers for combinatorial optimization problems, with the potential to outperform conventional approaches, provided that their hyperparameters are carefully tuned. Their temporal evolution is often described using time-continuous dynamics. However, most experimental implementations rely on measurement-feedback architectures that operate in a time-discrete manner. We observe that in such setups, the range of effective hyperparameters is substantially smaller than in the envisioned time-continuous analog Ising machine. In this paper, we analyze this discrepancy and discuss its impact on the practical operation of Ising machines. Next, we propose and experimentally verify a method to reduce the sensitivity to hyperparameter selection of these measurement-feedback architectures.

title: Electric current dynamics in the stellarator coil winding surface model
generated_summary:
This paper investigates the dynamics of electric current distributions on stellarator coil winding surfaces, providing rigorous mathematical characterizations of current flow behavior on toroidal and cylindrical surfaces relevant to fusion reactor design. The work is motivated by the observation that optimized current distributions on coil winding surfaces frequently exhibit centre and saddle-point regions, which complicate the translation of continuous current distributions into discrete coil designs.

The authors employ tools from dynamical systems theory, differential topology, and the theory of area-preserving flows to analyze divergence-free vector fields on surfaces. For toroidal surfaces, they establish a generic dichotomy: currents either have no zeros (yielding dense or uniformly periodic orbits) or possess zeros that necessarily produce centre and saddle-point structures. For cylindrical surfaces with oppositely oriented boundary currents, centre and saddle regions generically appear. Crucially, when physical constraints from Maxwell's equations are imposed—requiring currents to be both divergence-free and curl-free (harmonic Neumann fields)—the authors prove that such currents on cylindrical surfaces are either identically zero or everywhere non-vanishing with exclusively periodic poloidal orbits, eliminating problematic centre and saddle regions entirely.

These results are validated through numerical experiments showing that increasing Tikhonov regularization drives current distributions toward the harmonic regime. The findings have direct implications for stellarator coil optimization, particularly for emerging high-temperature superconductor technologies using cylindrical coil geometries, providing theoretical justification for regularization practices and informing engineering design choices.
original_abstract: In stellarator design, the coil winding surfaces $Σ\subset\mathbb R^3$ support current distributions $j$ that shape the magnetic field. This work provides a theoretical framework explaining the emergence of centre and saddle point regions, a key feature in coil optimisation. For coil winding surfaces with a toroidal shape, we prove a dichotomy principle: the current distribution has both centre and saddle point regions or is no-where vanishing. For coil winding surfaces that consist of piecewise cylinders, we show that if $j$ is oppositely oriented on the two boundary circles, centre and saddle points appear, and all but finitely many field lines of $j$ are periodic. When $j$ admits a harmonic potential, all field lines are closed poloidal orbits. These results offer insights into current patterns on winding surfaces, with implications for coil design strategies and their simplification.

title: Modified-gradient methods for exact divergence-free in meshless magnetohydrodynamics
generated_summary:
This paper presents a Lagrangian Godunov-type meshless modified-gradient (MG) method for magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) simulations that achieves exact divergence-free magnetic fields to machine precision. The method extends and modifies the existing constrained-gradient (CG) meshless framework by introducing a regularization on the reconstruction of the magnetic field at virtual interfaces, ensuring the divergence-free condition is maintained throughout simulations while preserving the conservative nature of the scheme.

The methodology builds upon Lagrangian meshless particle methods with Godunov-type Riemann solvers, modifying the gradient estimation procedure specifically for the magnetic field to enforce the solenoidal constraint. This approach avoids the need for divergence-cleaning schemes, which alter the MHD equations and may compromise conservation properties, and circumvents the difficulty of implementing constrained transport methods on unstructured or meshless discretizations.

Numerical experiments demonstrate that the MG method maintains global divergence-free conditions to machine precision across multiple test problems, including the Brio-Wu shock tube, field loop advection, Orszag-Tang vortex (in both 2D and 3D), magnetized blast wave, magnetic rotor, and magnetorotational instability. The method strongly reduces oscillations in the magnetic field, nearly eliminates advection errors, and ensures that the effective work from the Lorentz force vanishes as physically required, reducing dissipation in fluid quantities compared to the CG method.

The significance lies in providing a robust, conservative meshless MHD solver with exact divergence-free magnetic fields, though the authors note that solving the required large symmetric sparse linear systems presents computational efficiency challenges for massive-scale simulations.
original_abstract: We present a novel gradient regularization to completely eliminate the magnetic divergence error in meshless magnetohydrodynamics (MHD), which offers a high spatial resolution and conservative advantage, due to its Lagrangian nature. Comparing with the counterpart of constrained-gradient (CG) technique, we reform $\nabla \cdot \mathbf{B}=0$ by an implicit projection method to modify the magnetic-field gradients.   The accuracy of modified-gradient (MG) method is verified and it achieves exact divergence-free results with round-off precision, by using tests of shock tube, 2D and 3D vortex, magneto-rotational instability, and especially, advection experiment, compared with CG method and the GIZMO code. It leads to noticeable improvement in pattern, amplitude and numerical dissipation of divergence error of magnetic field.

title: Commissioning and Full Realization of the PLASEN System at BRIF

original_abstract: A PLASEN (Precision LAser Spectroscopy for Exotic Nuclei) system, consisting of a compact radio-frequency quadrupole cooler-buncher (RFQ-cb) and a collinear resonance ionization spectroscopy setup, has now been fully commissioned with radioactive ion beams at the Beijing Radioactive Ion-beam Facility (BRIF). Using both stable and radioactive Rb ion beams from BRIF, we demonstrated that the large beam energy spread observed at BRIF has been successfully handled by employing the RFQ-cb, enabling the delivery of high-quality bunched radioactive ion beams for collinear resonance ionization spectroscopy experiments. Under these conditions, we performed laser spectroscopy of exotic nuclei, achieving high resolution (about 100 MHz spectral linewidth) and high sensitivity (up to 1:200 efficiency). title: To trace or not to trace: analytical insights from network-based contact-tracing models
generated_summary:

The authors employ a pairwise approximation framework within an extended Susceptible-Infected-Tracing-Recovered (SITR) model, using the fast-variables approach to derive explicit epidemic threshold conditions. This method exploits early-time correlations that reach quasi-equilibrium rapidly, overcoming the limitations of standard linear stability analysis where closure relations become ill-defined at the disease-free steady state.

Key results reveal that assuming fast contact tracing can substantially underestimate the required tracing effort, sometimes by orders of magnitude. A minimum tracing coverage threshold exists below which no finite tracing rate can contain an epidemic. Network density non-linearly influences tracing effectiveness: denser networks require higher tracing rates, while overly sparse networks narrow the range of viable coverage levels. Triplewise tracing is consistently less efficient than pairwise tracing but contributes meaningfully when tracing timescales are comparable to disease progression.

These findings provide rigorous analytical foundations for designing realistic contact tracing strategies that account for operational delays, partial compliance, and network structure, with direct implications for public health planning during epidemics.
original_abstract: Contact tracing is one of the most important control measures deployed during epidemics. Relying on the identification of contacts of known infected individuals, it necessitates a network perspective. Although pairwise models have been used extensively to study contact tracing, their analysis typically depends on a decoupling assumption-most commonly that contact tracing operates on a much faster timescale than disease transmission. Furthermore, contact tracing models often assume that all infected individuals become contact tracing-triggering, which is unrealistic given partial compliance to treatment. We relax both of these restrictive assumptions and provide a full analytical characterisation of the epidemic threshold in the pairwise mean-field model. Our analysis uses a fast-variables approach that captures the rapid early stabilisation of key network quantities. Inspired by mechanisms from social adoption dynamics, we introduce triplewise contact tracing in which an infected individual can be traced not only through direct contact with a single tracing-triggering neighbor (pairwise tracing), but also indirectly when connected to two tracing-triggering nodes simultaneously. For pure pairwise and pure triplewise contact tracing, we derive analytical expressions for critical contact tracing levels and demonstrate that when many infected individuals bypass treatment, the epidemic can become uncontrollable. When both contact tracing mechanisms operate together, we map out their combined contribution and relative impact on epidemic control. This unified framework yields rigorous and tractable threshold conditions for contact tracing dynamics on networks, extending the applicability of pairwise models beyond the fast-tracing regime and providing new insight into the interplay between disease progression, partial treatment compliance, and higher-order tracing processes.

title: Capturing dual team properties with inclusion atoms
generated_summary:
This paper investigates the duality between downward and upward closed properties in propositional team-based logics.
