The work addresses four classes of team properties based on combinations of closure direction (downward vs. upward) and behavior with respect to the empty and full team.

The methodology centers on defining four propositional logics, each employing appropriate variants of inclusion atoms, and establishing their formal properties. For each logic, the author develops normal forms that reveal a surprisingly symmetric structure across the four systems. The paper demonstrates that each logic is expressively complete for the class of team properties with the relevant closure conditions, meaning every property satisfying the appropriate closure constraints can be expressed in the corresponding logic. Additionally, sound and complete natural deduction proof systems are provided for each of the four logics.

A notable finding is the close connection between the atoms used in logics for (quasi) upward closed properties and the "might" modalities studied in the existing literature. The paper also establishes strong compactness theorems for each logic, leveraging arguments from inquisitive logic adapted to the team semantics framework. This work enriches the landscape of propositional team logics by systematically addressing previously underexplored upward closed team properties.
original_abstract: We introduce propositional team-based logics expressively complete for (quasi) downward and (quasi) upward closed properties in a syntactically dual way, by using variants of the inclusion atom. In particular, the variants of the primitive inclusion atoms used in the (quasi) upward closed setting have equivalent formulas using variants of the might modality. The duality is visible in the logics' normal forms, mirroring the duality between the (quasi) upward and downward closed settings, where the quasi variants take special care of the empty and full team. Furthermore, we defined sound and complete natural deduction systems for each logic.

title: Local limits of uniform triangulations with boundaries in high genus
generated_summary:
This paper establishes local convergence results for uniform random triangulations with boundaries in the high genus regime, where both the number of vertices and the genus grow proportionally. The authors consider triangulations with multiple boundary components whose perimeters also grow to infinity, proving that when rooted at a typical edge on the boundary, these triangulations converge locally to supercritical half-plane triangulations from the Angel-Ray family. This confirms conjectures that these hyperbolic half-plane triangulations arise as local limits of finite high genus triangulations with boundaries.

The methodology relies on combinatorial estimates rather than exact enumeration formulas, making the approach robust and potentially applicable to other map models. A key innovation addresses the planarity of the local limit: the authors show that if a finite non-planar pattern appeared with positive probability, one could find many disjoint copies of it, and the resulting genus reduction would create a contradiction with volume estimates. The most technically challenging part involves excluding pathological boundary configurations where boundaries fold onto themselves or come close to other boundaries near the root.

The paper also generalizes a previous result by Budzinski and Louf, proving that rooting at a uniformly random edge yields convergence to the Planar Stochastic Hyperbolic Triangulation, now extended to the setting with boundaries. These results have implications for understanding peeling explorations and typical distances in high genus triangulations, potentially enabling more precise analysis of their logarithmic-scale geometry.
original_abstract: We study the local limits of uniform random triangulations with boundaries in the regime where the genus is proportional to the number of faces. Budzinski and Louf proved in 2020 that when there are no boundaries, the local limits exist and are the Planar Stochastic Hyperbolic Triangulation (PSHT) introduced in PSHT.   We show that when the triangulations considered have size n and boundaries with total length p that tends to infinity with n and p=o(n), the local limits around a typical boundary edge are the half-plane hyperbolic triangulations defined by Angel and Ray. This provides, for the first time, a construction of these hyperbolic half-plane triangulations as local limits of large genus triangulations.   We also prove that under the condition p = o(n), the local limit when rooted on a uniformly chosen oriented edge is given by the PSHT. Contrary to the proof of Budzinski and Louf, the latter does not rely on the Goulden-Jackson recurrence relation, but only on coarse combinatorial estimates. Thus, we expect that the proof can be adapted to local limits in similar models.

title: Chromatic thresholds for linear equations and recurrence
generated_summary:
This paper introduces and completely characterizes the chromatic threshold for homogeneous linear equations over prime cyclic groups, establishing a new structural dichotomy in additive combinatorics. For a homogeneous linear equation with coefficients summing to zero, the chromatic threshold measures how much density is needed in a solution-free set to force bounded chromatic number in the associated Cayley graph. The main result proves that the chromatic threshold vanishes if and only if the equation possesses a zero-sum subcollection of coefficients of size at least three.

The proof employs two distinct methodological approaches. For the forward direction, the authors use Fourier analysis and supersaturation: the zero-sum sub-equation on at least three variables forces structural constraints on dense solution-free sets via Bohr set analysis, enabling a bounded coloring through spectral discretization. For the reverse direction, they develop a novel topological obstruction by introducing a generalized Kneser graph whose chromatic number is bounded below using an equivariant Borsuk–Ulam argument, then embed this graph into appropriate Cayley graphs while maintaining solution-freeness through careful arithmetic constructions over product groups.

A key byproduct resolves a question of Griesmer on Hamming ball Cayley graphs over odd-characteristic groups and establishes a complete separation between topological and measurable recurrence in every infinite discrete abelian group. The chromatic threshold condition sits strictly between Roth-type density regularity and Rado-type partition regularity, revealing a new intermediate structural phenomenon connecting extremal graph theory, additive combinatorics, and topological dynamics.
original_abstract: Motivated by classical problems in extremal graph theory, we study a chromatic analogue of Roth-type questions for linear equations over $\mathbb F_p$. Given a homogeneous equation $\mathcal L:\sum_{i=1}^k c_i x_i=0$ with $k\ge 3$, we study $\mathcal L$-solution-free sets $A\subseteq \mathbb F_p$ through the chromatic number of the Cayley graph $\mathsf{Cay}(\mathbb F_p,A)$. We introduce the \emph{chromatic threshold} $δ_χ(\mathcal L)$, the minimum density that guarantees bounded chromatic number of $\mathsf{Cay}(\mathbb F_p,A)$ among all $\mathcal L$-solution-free sets $A$, and determine exactly when $δ_χ(\mathcal L)=0$. We prove that $δ_χ(\mathcal L)=0$ if and only if $\mathcal L$ contains a zero-sum subcollection of at least three coefficients.   A key ingredient is a quantitative chromatic lower bound for Cayley graphs on $\mathbb Z_p^n$ generated by Hamming balls around the all-ones vector. This is obtained by introducing a new Kneser-type graph that admits a natural embedding into $\mathbb Z_p^n$, together with an equivariant Borsuk--Ulam type argument. As a consequence, we resolve a question of Griesmer. We further relate our classification to the hierarchy of measurable, topological, and Bohr recurrence. In particular, we show that every infinite discrete abelian group admits a set that is topological recurrent but not measurable recurrent, extending the seminal examples of Kříž and Ruzsa.

title: Thresholds for colouring the random Borsuk graph
generated_summary:
## Summary

This paper investigates the chromatic number of random Borsuk graphs, a geometric random graph model where vertices are randomly sampled on the unit sphere in d-dimensional space, and edges connect pairs of vertices whose distance exceeds a threshold parameter. The random Borsuk graph combines elements of random geometric graphs with the classical Borsuk graph, whose chromatic number is related to the famous Borsuk conjecture concerning the partition of sets into pieces of smaller diameter.

The main contribution is establishing sharp thresholds for the chromatic number of random Borsuk graphs as a function of the dimension, the number of vertices, and the distance parameter. The authors determine the regimes in which the chromatic number undergoes phase transitions, identifying precise conditions under which the graph can be properly colored with a given number of colors. The methodology combines probabilistic techniques from random graph theory with geometric and topological arguments, including tools from combinatorial topology such as the Borsuk-Ulam theorem, which provides lower bounds on the chromatic number.

Key results include characterizing when the chromatic number equals specific values and identifying the threshold behavior as parameters vary. The significance of this work lies in bridging combinatorial topology and probabilistic combinatorics, providing new insights into how geometric and topological constraints interact with randomness to determine graph coloring properties. These results contribute to the broader understanding of chromatic thresholds in geometric random graph models.
original_abstract: We consider the chromatic number of the random Borsuk graph. The random Borsuk graph is obtained by sampling $n$ points i.i.d. uniformly at random on the $d$-dimensional sphere $S^d$, and joining a pair of points by an edge whenever their geodesic distance is $>π-α$ where the parameter $α=α(n)$ may depend on $n$. Kahle and Martinez-Figueroa have shown that the switch from being $(d+1)$-colourable to needing $\geq d+2$ colours occurs in the regime where the average degree is of logarithmic order. We show that for each $2\leq k\leq d$, the switch from being $k$-colourable to needing $> k$ colours occurs in the regime when the average degree is constant. What is more, we show that for $k=2$ there is a sharp threshold of the form $α(n) = c \cdot n^{-1/d}$, where the constant $c$ can be expressed in terms of the critical intensity for continuum AB percolation on $\mathbb{R}^d$. For $k=3,\dots,d+1$ we show that there is a sharp threshold for "almost all $n$".

title: Obata's rigidity theorem in free probability
generated_summary:
This paper establishes a free probability analogue of Obata's rigidity theorem, demonstrating that extremizers of Voiculescu's free Poincaré inequality under a non-commutative curvature-dimension condition must exhibit rigid algebraic structure. The work draws inspiration from the classical Cheng–Zhou splitting theorem, which shows that spaces saturating the Poincaré inequality under curvature-dimension bounds must split off a Gaussian factor.

The authors introduce a non-commutative curvature condition formulated through bounds on the non-commutative Hessian of conjugate variables, working within the framework of Lipschitz conjugate variables developed by Dabrowski. Under this condition, they establish that the free Poincaré constant is controlled by the inverse of the convexity parameter, paralleling the classical Bakry–Émery theory. The methodology employs a weak-L² Bakry–Émery type argument adapted to the tracial setting, leveraging key commutation relations between generators and free difference quotients.

The central result shows that under the curvature-dimension condition, any function saturating the free Poincaré inequality must be affine linear in the generators, forcing the appearance of a semicircular direction after normalization. This yields a free product decomposition of the underlying von Neumann algebra, where the semicircular direction generates a maximal amenable subalgebra by Popa's theorem. The work addresses a significant gap in understanding free functional inequalities beyond the semicircular case and suggests that a comprehensive free Bakry–Émery theory with connections to random matrix models and von Neumann algebra structure theory is within reach.
original_abstract: We establish a free analogue of Obata's rigidity theorem. More precisely, Cheng and Zhou (2017) proved that on a weighted Riemannian manifold, the sharp spectral gap (Poincaré constant) is achieved only when the space splits isometrically off a one-dimensional Gaussian factor, providing an infinite-dimensional counterpart of Obata's rigidity theorem. We obtain the corresponding phenomenon in free probability, extending it beyond the setting of analytic self-adjoint potentials:   Assume a self-adjoint $n$-tuple $X=(X_1,\dots,X_n)$ admits Lipschitz conjugate variables in the sense of Dabrowski (2014). Under a suitable non-commutative curvature-dimension condition, we show that any non-zero saturator of Voiculescu's free Poincaré inequality must be an affine function of the generators. Consequently, we deduce that the von Neumann algebra $M=W^*(X_1,\dots,X_n)$ necessarily splits off a freely complemented semicircular component $W^*(Y_1)\simeq L^{\infty}([-2,2],μ_{\rm sc})$, which is also maximal amenable in $M$.   More generally, whenever the first eigenspace of the free Laplacian $Δ=\partial^*\bar\partial$ is finite-dimensional of rank $r\ge 1$, our rigidity argument shows that these $r$ extremal directions form a free semicircular family, yielding a free product decomposition with an $L(\mathbb{F}_r)$ factor. This provides a free-probability analogue of the classical Gaussian splitting phenomenon and reveals a rigidity mechanism under non-commutative curvature.

title: The Inverse Micromechanics Problem given Dielectric Constants for Isotropic Composites with Spherical Inclusions
generated_summary:
This paper addresses the inverse micromechanics problem of determining volumetric fractions of components in isotropic composite materials with spherical inclusions, given complex dielectric constant measurements. The main contribution is the novel application of convex optimization to Eshelby-based inverse micromechanics, replacing computationally expensive evolutionary algorithms like simulated annealing.

The authors formulate the inverse problem using the Eshelby-Mori-Tanaka mean-field averaging model for dielectric permittivity. They prove that the inverse problem is strictly quasiconvex for two-component composites and quasiconvex for multi-component composites, enabling the use of efficient convex optimization techniques. A multi-frequency formulation is developed using the Charnes-Cooper change of variables and epigraph reformulation, converting the problem into a linear program. Requirements for accurate solutions are characterized through the rank and minimum singular value of a constraint sensitivity matrix.

The approach is validated on three material systems using forward-computed dielectric constants. Key findings demonstrate that the presence of a strongly dispersive component significantly improves volumetric prediction accuracy with fewer frequency measurements. Increasing the number of measurement frequencies improves both the optimal objective value and the minimum singular value of the constraint sensitivity matrix, enhancing prediction robustness.

The significance of this work lies in establishing a computationally efficient, mathematically rigorous framework for determining volumetric compositions from dielectric measurements, with potential applications in nondestructive evaluation of composite materials. The framework can potentially be extended to more complex microstructures through the concept of equivalent microstructures.
original_abstract: In this article, convex optimization is introduced as a promising tool to study Eshelby based inverse micromechanics problems. The focus is on inverse micromechanics using the Eshelby-Mori-Tanaka model given the dielectric constants of the composite material and of all of its components. The model is exactly the same for the conductivity properties as well. This choice of model is made since the model is fairly simple and has a closed form analytical solution for the case of spheroidal inclusions as well. The forward or direct micromechanics problem deals with the determination of effective properties of a composite material given the properties of its components and microstructural information. The focus is on isotropic composites and the distribution of inclusions is assumed to be such that this holds. The inverse micromechanics problem considered in this paper deals with the determination of microstructural information given the properties of the composite material and all of its components. Since in this paper, isotropy of the composite and only spherical inclusions are considered, the goal is to determine just volume fractions of the components of the composite material. The inverse problem is formulated as a Linear Programming problem and is solved. Before this, the inverse problem and certain important variants of it are examined through the lens of convex optimization. Lastly, promising results regarding the relationship between dispersive materials, noise in measurements, and quality of obtained volumetric splits are showcased. The scope of the use of convex optimization in inverse micromechanics is discussed.

title: A complete classification of modular compactifications of the universal Jacobian
generated_summary:
This paper provides a complete classification of all modular compactifications of the universal Jacobian over the moduli stack of stable pointed curves. The universal Jacobian parametrizes line bundles on smooth curves, and understanding its compactifications over the boundary of the moduli space of curves has been a central problem in algebraic geometry for over thirty years.

The authors introduce "V-functions," which are combinatorial objects defined on "half-vine graphs" encoding the topological types of biconnected subcurves. These functions must satisfy compatibility conditions arising from complementary subcurves and "triangle" degenerations. The main result establishes an anti-isomorphism between the poset of compactified universal Jacobian stacks and the poset of V-functions, extending previous classifications that addressed only the fine (non-degenerate) case. The methodology builds on the theory of torsion-free sheaves, good moduli spaces, and V-stability conditions for families of nodal curves.

Key additional results include: a complete characterization of when two compactified universal Jacobians are isomorphic, showing this occurs precisely when their V-functions lie in the same orbit under a natural group action; a description of "classical" compactifications arising from numerical polarizations; a resolution of singularities of universal families via compactified Jacobians over curves with one additional marked point; and a detailed analysis of maximal and submaximal elements in the poset structure.

These results have broad implications for studying wall-crossing phenomena, Brill-Noether theory, double ramification cycles, and the birational geometry of moduli spaces of curves.
original_abstract: We classify all modular compactifications of the universal Jacobian over $\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{g,n}$, both as stacks and as their relative good moduli spaces. Our main result gives a combinatorial parametrization of compactified universal Jacobian stacks by $V$-functions on a stability domain $\mathbb{D}_{g,n}$ of half-vine types (two-components topological types with a chosen side); under this correspondence, fine compactifications are exactly the general $V$-functions.   We single out the classical compactified universal Jacobians, namely those induced by numerical polarizations (relative $\mathbb{R}$-line bundles on the universal curve $\overline{\mathcal{C}}_{g,n}/\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{g,n}$), recovering the constructions of Kass-Pagani and Melo in the fine case, and we prove that their good moduli spaces are locally projective over $\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{g,n}$.   We determine when two compactified universal Jacobians are isomorphic over $\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{g,n}$ and describe a resolution of the universal family via a compactified Jacobian over $\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{g,n+1}$.   Finally, we analyse the poset $Σ_{g,n}$ of compactified universal Jacobians, an extension of the poset of regions of the hyperplane arrangement of classical stability conditions $\mathcal{A}_{g,n}$ studied in Kass-Pagani. We prove that for $n=0$ all compactified universal Jacobians are those constructed by Caporaso. We then give an explicit description of the submaximal elements of $Σ_{g,n}$ for all $n$, generalizing the stability walls in the classical stability space $\mathcal{A}_{g,n}$ from Kass-Pagani's work.

title: Cross-free families have linear size
generated_summary:
This paper resolves a long-standing conjecture of Karzanov and Lomonosov by proving that *k*-cross-free families on an *n*-element ground set have linear size for every fixed *k*. A family of sets is *k*-cross-free if it contains no *k* pairwise crossing members, where two sets cross if all four regions of their Venn diagram are nonempty. The conjecture, dating to 1978, posited that the maximum size of such a family is O(*n*), but for general *k* ≥ 4, only an O(*n* log *n*) bound was known, established by Kupavskii, Pach, and Tomon in 2019. Prior to that, the best bound was O(*n*^(2⌊*k*/2⌋−2)), which had stood for decades.

The main theorem establishes that for every *k* ≥ 2, there exists a constant *c*(*k*) such that any *k*-cross-free family on an *n*-element ground set has size at most *c*(*k*) · *n*. The proof employs a structural approach involving cross-support trees, where nodes represent chains of sets, enabling a hierarchical decomposition of the family.

This result has significant implications across multiple areas. It originated from the locking theorem characterizing families lockable by multiflows, generalizing the max-flow min-cut theorem. It also connects to geometric crossing problems, extending the known linear bound for families of intervals on cyclically ordered sets to arbitrary set families, and has applications in phylogenetic combinatorics and split systems.
original_abstract: Two subsets $A$ and $B$ of a ground set $X$ are \emph{crossing} if none of the four sets $A\setminus B,B\setminus A,A\cap B, X\setminus (A\cup B)$ are empty. Almost fifty years ago, Karzanov and Lomonosov conjectured that every family of subsets of an $n$-element ground set with no $k$-pairwise crossing members has size $O(kn)$. We prove the bound $O_k(n)$, settling (arguably) the main problem about the growth rate of such families.

title: Homological methods in rigidity theory using graphs of groups
generated_summary:
This paper advances the theory of graph-of-groups realisations as a unified framework for structural rigidity theory, addressing the open question of when necessary counting conditions for rigidity are also sufficient. The main contribution is a genericity result proving that for sufficiently generic graph-of-groups realisations with zero-dimensional stabilisers, rigidity is fully characterised by a combinatorial counting condition analogous to the Geiringer-Laman theorem.

The methodology relies on homological algebra applied to cellular sheaves on graphs. Infinitesimal motions are modeled as the first cohomology group of sheaves, and long exact sequences are employed to study how inductive graph constructions—specifically extensions characterized by a result of Frank and Szegő—preserve independence. The authors introduce "motion sheaves" and "associated sheaves," showing that their cohomology dimensions exhibit upper semi-continuity with respect to the Zariski topology on naturally defined algebraic varieties (products of Grassmannians). A geometric analysis demonstrates that graph-of-groups realisations with zero-dimensional stabilisers cut out full-dimensional semi-algebraic subsets within these varieties, ensuring they behave like generic motion sheaves.

The results recover the classical Geiringer-Laman theorem for two-dimensional bar-joint rigidity and extend immediately to spherical, hyperbolic, and parallel rigidity settings. The work provides a general mechanism for realising sparsity matroids and establishes new connections between homological methods, Lie group theory, and combinatorial rigidity, opening promising avenues for studying higher-dimensional rigidity problems.
original_abstract: In recent work, Stokes and Vermant considered graph-of-groups realisations of hypergraphs as a new description of rigidity-theoretic problems. In this paper, we show that the infinitesimal aspects of graph-of-groups realisations can be analysed using cellular sheaves and their cohomology. Using these tools, we give an algebraic condition for Henneberg moves to preserve independence, and we prove that the infinitesimal rigidity and flexibility of certain graph-of-groups realisations are generic properties. We use these results to show that whenever a rigidity-theoretic problem is defined in a real algebraic group $G$ using a $1$-dimensional connected subgroup $H$ with $N_{G}(H)/H$ finite, then the so-called Maxwell-count leads to a necessary and sufficient condition for minimal rigidity, generalising various known results in the literature.

title: Structured distance to singularity as a nonlinear system of equations
generated_summary:
This paper presents a novel method for computing the structured distance to singularity, a classical matrix nearness problem that seeks the smallest perturbation making a matrix singular while preserving its structure (such as sparsity patterns or Toeplitz form). Unlike the unstructured case, where the distance equals the smallest singular value via the Eckart-Young-Mirsky theorem, the structured problem is considerably more challenging since minimal structured perturbations are generally not rank one.

The authors reformulate the structured distance to singularity as a system of nonlinear equations, which they solve using Newton's method with backtracking line search. This approach avoids the nested optimization procedures required by two existing methods: the ODE-based gradient system approach and the structured low-rank approximation (SLRA)/Riemann-Oracle method. The paper first provides a detailed theoretical comparison between these two existing methods, identifying parallels between their optimization procedures, before introducing the new formulation. A key observation underlying the work is that minimal structured perturbations can be obtained as orthogonal projections of rank-one matrices onto the structure space.

The method is tested on both large sparse matrices and smaller problems with Toeplitz-like structures. The computational procedure requires only matrix-vector multiplications with structured matrices and vector inner products, making it practical for large-scale problems. The significance of this work lies in providing a more direct computational approach that eliminates nested iterations, with potential extensions to distance-to-stability problems and other manifold-constrained matrix nearness problems.
original_abstract: In this article we study the structured distance to singularity for a nonsingular matrix $A\in\mathbb{C}^{n\times n}$, with a prescribed linear structure $\mathcal{S}$ (for instance, a sparsity pattern, or a real Toeplitz structure), i.e., the norm of the smallest perturbation $Δ\in \mathcal{S}$, such that $A + Δ$ is singular. This is an example of structured matrix nearness problem: a family of problems that arise in control and systems theory and in numerical analysis, when characterizing the robustness of a certain property of a system with respect to perturbations that are constrained to a certain structure (for example the structure of the nominal system). We start by highlighting the parallelism between two main tools which have been proposed in the literature: a gradient system approach for a functional in the eigenvalues, which requires the solution of certain low-rank matrix differential equations (see [Guglielmi, Lubich, Sicilia, SINUM 2023]), and a two-level optimization approach in which the inner linear least-squares problem is solved explicitly (see [Usevich, Markovsky, JCAM 2014] and [Gnazzo, Noferini, Nyman, Poloni, FoCM 2025]). In particular, these articles underline the remarkable property that $Δ$ is (at least generically) the orthogonal projection onto the structure $\mathcal{S}$ of a rank-1 matrix $uv^*$. This property and the parallelism suggest a new reformulation of the problem into a system of nonlinear equations in the two vector unknowns $u,v \in\mathbb{C}^n$. We study this new formulation, and propose an algorithm to solve these nonlinear equations directly with the multivariate Newton's method. We discuss how to avoid the singularity of such system of nonlinear equations, and how to ensure monotonic convergence. The resulting algorithm is faster than the existing ones for large matrices, and maintains comparable accuracy.

title: Four relations on the set of point-hyperplane anti-flags
generated_summary:
This paper investigates four natural relations defined on the set of point-hyperplane anti-flags (pairs of non-incident points and hyperplanes) in projective spaces over arbitrary fields. The four relations correspond to the four possible geometric arrangements of two anti-flags. When the field characteristic differs from two, each anti-flag can be identified with an involution in the projective general linear group, and two of the relations correspond to cases where the associated involutions either commute or compose to yield a transvection.

The main contribution is a structural result showing that each of the four relations can be recovered from any other, with a single exception: when the projective space is three-dimensional over the field of two elements and one attempts to recover a specific relation from another. We consider the corresponding relations on the set of such anti-flags and show that each of them can be recovered from any other except in one special case. If the field consists of two elements, then one of the relations cannot be used to recover each of the remaining three. title: On spiral steady flows for the Couette-Taylor problem

original_abstract: We investigate the Couette-Taylor problem for a steady incompressible viscous fluid in a 3D cylindrical annulus, where one of the two cylinders is still, under both Dirichlet and boundary conditions involving the vorticity that naturally appear in the weak formulation. The outcome of this study is twofold. First, we explicitly determine all the solutions with a specific geometric \emph{partial invariance}, which coincide with the so-called spiral Poiseuille or Poiseuille-Couette flows depending on the boundary conditions. Second, for small boundary data, we provide stability of such solutions, that is, no steady finite-energy perturbations are admissible. title: Existence and regularity for an entire Grushin-Choquard equation

original_abstract: We consider the following Choquard equation   $$   -Δ_γu + u = \left(d(z)^{-μ} \ast |u|^p\right)|u|^{p-2}u, \text{ in } \mathbb{R}^N,   $$   where $Δ_γ$ is the Grushin operator. We also establish that the solutions belong to $L^q(\mathbb{R}^N)$ for all $q\in [2,\infty]$ and to $C^{0,α}_\mathrm{loc}(\mathbb{R}^N)$ for some $α\in (0,1)$.

title: Controlled fields, rough stochastic calculus, and Itô-Wentzell-Alekseev-Gröbner identities

original_abstract: We develop a calculus of space-time controlled fields for rough stochastic systems. This approach provides a unified composition rule for evaluating random fields along rough semimartingales and yields a rough stochastic Itô-Wentzell formula under natural and verifiable regularity assumptions. Our motivation comes from works of Hudde et al. (2024) and, independently, Del Moral and Singh (2022) where the authors established, respectively, Itô-Alekseev-Gröbner, backward Itô-Wentzell, and diffusion interpolation formulas.

title: Weighted Sobolev Inequalities via the Meyers--Ziemer Framework: Measures, Isoperimetric Inequalities, and Endpoint Estimates

original_abstract: We establish a new global endpoint Sobolev inequality for measures that extends the classical theorem of Meyers-Ziemer by placing a maximal function on the right-hand side. This result has several significant consequences. It extends naturally to functions of weighted bounded variation and yields corresponding capacity and isoperimetric inequalities. The inequality is also closely connected to endpoint estimates for fractional operators, including bounds for fractional maximal functions and Hardy space endpoint estimates for the Riesz potential. Our main inequality yields a family of endpoint inequalities, characterized in terms of subrepresentation formulas, Lorentz space improvements, and isoperimetric inequalities for measures and bounded open sets. When one moves away from the endpoint to $p>1$, the analogous inequalities no longer hold in general; however, we identify a sharp bumped maximal function for which the corresponding non-endpoint inequality is valid. Finally, we show that this framework yields new $(p,p)$ two-weight Sobolev inequalities.

title: Integral Formulation and the Brézis-Ekeland-Nayroles-Type Principle for Prox-Regular Sweeping Processes

original_abstract: We study sweeping processes in a Hilbert space driven by time-dependent uniformly prox-regular sets, allowing the moving constraint to exhibit discontinuities of bounded variation. We introduce a new integral formulation for bounded-variation trajectories, given by a global variational inequality tested against continuous admissible trajectories, and we compare it with the standard differential-measure formulation, in which the differential measure of the trajectory is constrained by the proximal normal cone. In the prox-regular (generally nonconvex) framework, the variational inequality necessarily includes a quadratic correction term reflecting the hypomonotonicity of proximal normal cones.   Under mild regularity assumptions on the moving set, including lower semicontinuity in time, uniform prox-regularity of the values, and a selection-extension property guaranteeing a rich class of test trajectories (satisfied, for instance, in the convex case and for bounded prox-regular sets), we prove that the new integral formulation is equivalent to the differential-measure formulation. This yields a unified bounded-variation notion of solution for prox-regular sweeping processes.   We further establish a Brézis-Ekeland-Nayroles-type variational characterization via a prox-regular variational residual: the residual is nonpositive along every admissible trajectory, and solutions are exactly those trajectories for which this residual attains its maximal value, namely zero. As a consequence, we prove a stability result: a uniform limit of admissible trajectories with vanishing residual is a solution of the limit sweeping process. The resulting variational framework provides a robust tool for stability and approximation analyses in the prox-regular, nonconvex setting.

title: A Knebusch trace formula for Azumaya algebras with involution

original_abstract: We establish a trace formula for signatures of hermitian forms over Azumaya algebras with involution, extending Knebusch's work on symmetric bilinear forms over finite étale extensions of commutative base rings. As an application when the base ring is semilocal, we obtain an exact sequence for total signatures, related to Pfister's local-global principle and the notion of stability index.

title: Conditional asymptotic stability of solitary waves of the Euler-Poisson system on the line

original_abstract: We apply the idea of using a combination of virial inequalities and Kato smoothing, previously applied to NLS and generalized KdV pure power equations to Euler-Poisson: we assume that a solution remains very close for all times to a soliton in an appropriate space and then we prove an asymptotic convergence to a soliton for $t\to +\infty$.

title: The Extra Vanishing Structure and Nonlinear Stability of Multi-Dimensional Rarefaction Waves: The Geometric Weighted Energy Estimates

original_abstract: We study the resolution of discontinuous singularities in gas dynamics via multi-dimensional rarefaction waves. In this paper, we establish the nonlinear stability of multi-dimensional rarefaction waves for the compressible Euler equations with ideal gas law. We prove that for initial data being small perturbations of the planar rarefaction wave in $H^s$ ($s > s_c$), there exists a unique global solution that converges asymptotically to the background rarefaction wave as $t \to \infty$. Our proof relies on a novel Geometric Weighted Energy Method (GWEM), which yields stable energy estimates without loss of derivatives in standard Sobolev spaces, overcoming the limitations of previous Nash-Moser schemes. A key ingredient is a detailed geometric description of the rarefaction wave fronts via the acoustical metric, where we identify a hidden extra vanishing structure in the top-order derivatives of the characteristic speed. This is the first paper in a series, providing the crucial a priori energy bounds. The existence of solutions and applications to the multi-dimensional Riemann problem will be addressed in the forthcoming companion paper.

title: Teichmüller space of a closed set in the Riemann sphere

These results deepen the understanding of how holomorphic motions and Teichmüller theory interact, with implications for the study of quasiconformal mappings and deformation theory of Riemann surfaces.
original_abstract: The Teichmüller space of a closed set in the Riemann sphere is a simply connected complex Banach manifold. Its complex structure follows from Lieb isomorphism. In this paper, we show the conformal naturality of Lieb isomorphism. We then study Douady-Earle section for these Teichmüller spaces. In particular, we study the real-analyticity of Douady-Earle section for classical Teichmüller spaces. We give two explicit examples of maximal holomorphic motions over simply connected complex Banach manifolds. As an application of the real-analyticity of the Douady-Earle section for the classical Teichmüller spaces of Riemann surfaces, we prove a new result showing that a family of Jordan curves varies real-analytically over a simply connected complex Banach manifold and as quasiconformal images of the one at the basepoint, provided that a finite number of marked points on the Jordan curves vary holomorphically over the same parameter space.

title: Dyson Brownian motion on a Jordan curve

The work provides a natural dynamical framework for studying confined planar Coulomb gases and Fekete point distributions on curves, bridging stochastic processes, potential theory, and statistical mechanics.
original_abstract: Zabrodin recently proposed a generalization of Dyson Brownian motion to a setting where the particles are confined to a smooth Jordan curve in the plane. In this paper, we discuss a rigorous construction of such a process on a rectifiable Jordan curve and study some of its basic properties. Under further smoothness assumptions, we derive the associated Fokker-Planck-Kolmogorov equation, prove convergence towards the stationary Coulomb gas distribution, study large deviations at low temperature, and derive the limiting mean-field McKean--Vlasov equation in the many-particle limit.

title: Maximum of sparsely equicorrelated Gaussian fields and applications

original_abstract: We investigate the extreme values of a sparse and equicorrelated Gaussian field on a triangle: the correlations on every vertical or horizontal line are all equal to a parameter $r \in [0,1/2]$ and are zero everywhere else. This problem is closely linked with various problems in high-dimensional statistics and extreme-value theory. We identify the threshold for $r$ at which the standard Gumbel law breaks down. Our result is based on a subtle application of the Chen-Stein method for Poisson approximation. As applications, we discuss the implication of our results on multiple testing and resolve several questions that were left open in \cite{heiny2024maximum}, \cite{tang2022asymptotic} and \cite{Jiang19}.

title: Andrews--Gordon type identities with parity restrictions through particle motion

original_abstract: In this paper, we use the particle motion bijection introduced by Warnaar and developed by the two authors, Jouhet and Konan, to study q-series and partition identities of the Andrews--Gordon type with parity restrictions. These restrictions are of the type ``even (resp. odd) parts appear an even number of times". We prove $q$-series identities where a multisum equals a sum of products, which generalise identities of Andrews and Kim--Yee in a similar way that Stanton's identities generalised the Andrews--Gordon identities. As a consequence of our results, we obtain a simple proof of a recent identity of Chern--Li--Stanton--Xue--Yee related to Ariki--Koike algebras.

title: Besov regularity of solutions to the Dirichlet problem for the Bessel $(p,s)$-Laplacian

original_abstract: We study the Dirichlet problem for a class of fractional $p$-Laplacian operators of order $s \in (0,1)$ defined through the Riesz fractional gradient, which differs fundamentally from the standard fractional $p$-Laplacian. Our analysis combines the framework of Lions-Calderón spaces, Besov embeddings, and an adaptation of Nirenberg's difference quotient method, originally developed by Savaré, to the fractional Riesz setting. As a main result, we establish global Besov regularity estimates for weak solutions. Concretely, in the superquadratic regime $p \geq 2$, we prove $u \in \dot{B}_{p,\infty}^{s+1/p}(Ω)$ for $s \in [\frac{1}{p'},1)$, and $u \in \dot{B}_{p,\infty}^{s+\frac{s}{p-1}}(Ω)$ for $s \in (0,\frac{1}{p'})$. In the subquadratic case $1<p<2$, we show $u \in \dot{B}_{p,\infty}^{s+1/2}(Ω)$ for $s \in [\frac{1}{2},1)$, and $u \in \dot{B}_{p,\infty}^{2s}(Ω)$ for $s \in (0,\frac12)$, with quantitative bounds depending on the source data.

title: On Ehrhart theory for tropical vector bundles

Additionally, for the tautological tropical vector bundle associated to any matroid, they prove that the rank of global sections equals the Euler characteristic, which they interpret as vanishing of higher cohomologies—consistent with known results in the representable case. The paper also extends Klyachko's split resolution construction to tropical vector bundles. This work bridges tropical geometry, matroid theory, and toric geometry, providing foundational tools for the still-developing theory of higher-rank tropical vector bundles.
original_abstract: The notion of a tropical vector bundle on a toric variety was recently introduced by Khan-Maclagan and Kaveh-Manon. In this paper, we study the Euler characteristic and rank of global sections for tropical vector bundles. We associate a convex chain (a finite integer linear combination of indicator functions of convex polytopes) to a tropical vector bundle encoding its Euler characteristic. We then see that the Khovanskii-Pukhlikov theory of convex chains gives a combinatorial Hirzebruch-Riemann-Roch theorem for tropical vector bundles. This, in particular, applies to toric vector bundles. Also, we extend Klyachko's resolution of a toric vector bundle by split toric vector bundles to tropical vector bundles. As shown by Kaveh-Manon, every matroid comes with a tautological tropical vector bundle. We answer positively a question posed by Kaveh-Manon about equality of Euler characteristic with rank of space of global sections (in other words, vanishing of higher cohomologies) for the tautological bundle of a matroid.

title: Worst-case $L_p$-approximation of periodic functions using median lattice algorithms
generated_summary:
This paper investigates worst-case approximation of periodic functions in weighted Korobov spaces using a randomized median lattice algorithm, extending previous analyses to the full range of Lp norms for 2 ≤ p ≤ ∞. The main contribution is establishing high-probability, nearly optimal convergence rates for Lp-approximation using median aggregation of multiple independent rank-1 lattice rules.

The methodology employs a randomized algorithm that approximates Fourier coefficients on a weighted hyperbolic-cross-type index set using multiple independent rank-1 lattice rules with a prime number of points, then takes the componentwise median across repetitions. The proof strategy combines known error bounds for L2-approximation and L∞-approximation with a norm interpolation inequality to obtain results for general Lp spaces.

The key result demonstrates that this median lattice algorithm achieves, with high probability, convergence rates that match the optimal rates for linear sampling algorithms, up to logarithmic factors associated with hyperbolic-cross truncation and an arbitrarily small loss parameter. Notably, in the L2 endpoint case, the constants are shown to be independent of dimension under standard summability conditions on the product weights, reflecting favorable tractability properties known from related integration settings.

The significance of this work lies in connecting the robust median aggregation principle—increasingly used in randomized quasi-Monte Carlo integration—to the approximation setting, providing a unified framework that yields sharp tail estimates across all Lp norms without requiring precise knowledge of smoothness parameters.
original_abstract: We study the worst-case approximation of multivariate periodic functions from the weighted Korobov space $H_{d,α,γ}$ with smoothness $α>1/2$ in the Lebesgue norm $L_p([0,1]^d)$ for $1\le p\le\infty$. We analyze a \emph{median lattice algorithm} that reconstructs a truncated Fourier series by approximating the coefficients on a hyperbolic-cross-type index set using $R$ rank-1 lattice sampling rules with independent randomly chosen generating vectors, and then aggregating the resulting coefficient estimators via the componentwise median. For an odd number of repetitions $R>1$ and an odd prime lattice size $N$, we prove high-probability error bounds in both $L_\infty$ and $L_2$. Interpolation then yields the result for all $1 \le p\le\infty$. In particular, with a high probability, the algorithm satisfies \[ \mathrm{err}(H_{d,α,γ},L_p,A)\ \le\ C_{d,α,β,\boldsymbolγ,p}\, N^{- α+ (\frac12 - \frac1p)_+ + β}, \qquad 1 \le p\le\infty,\ β>0, \] where $(x)_+ = \max\{x, 0\}$, $N$ is the number of function evaluations, and the weights $\boldsymbolγ$ and the constant $C_{d,α,β,\boldsymbolγ,p}$ are independent of $N$. For $p=\infty$, $C_{d,α,β,\boldsymbolγ,\infty}$ is dimension-independent under the summability condition $\sum_{j=1}^\infty γ_j^{1/(2α)}<\infty$. These results extend recent analyses of median-based lattice approximation in $L_2$ and complement related multiple-shift lattice approaches, showing that median aggregation yields nearly optimal $L_p$-approximation rates (up to logarithmic factors and an arbitrarily small loss) in weighted Korobov spaces.

title: Hitting time for Hamilton cycles in pseudorandom graphs
generated_summary:
This paper resolves a longstanding question posed by Frieze and Krivelevich (2002) concerning the hitting time for Hamilton cycles in random graph processes on pseudorandom graphs. The authors prove that for any (n, d, λ)-graph (an n-vertex, d-regular graph with second eigenvalue at most λ) with sufficiently large spectral ratio d/λ, the hitting time for Hamiltonicity coincides with the hitting time for minimum degree at least 2 with high probability. Unlike all previous results, which required the degree d to be polynomially large in n, this result only requires d/λ to exceed a sufficiently large constant.

The methodology combines structural analysis of the hitting time graph with a novel extension of recent breakthrough techniques on Hamiltonicity in expanders. The authors show the hitting time graph decomposes into a large core with strong expansion properties and a small, scattered set of low-degree vertices. A key technical contribution, potentially of independent interest, establishes that expanders contain Hamilton cycles even when forced to include specific well-separated prescribed edges, proved via adaptations of Posá rotation and sorting network techniques.

As corollaries, the authors establish sharp thresholds for Hamiltonicity in random subgraphs of (n, d, λ)-graphs and extend results to k edge-disjoint Hamilton cycles for k up to d/(Cλ). These results provide the strongest possible characterization—pinpointing the exact moment random subgraphs of pseudorandom graphs become Hamiltonian—and substantially advance understanding of Hamiltonicity in sparse random-like graphs.
original_abstract: Consider the random subgraph process on a base graph $G$ with $n$ vertices: we generate a sequence $\{G_t\}_{t=0}^{|E(G)|}$ by taking a uniformly random ordering of the edges of $G$ and then adding these edges one by one to the empty graph $G_0$ on the same vertex set. We prove that there is a constant $C > 0$ such that if $G$ is an $(n,d,λ)$-graph with $d/λ\ge C$, then with high probability, the hitting time for the appearance of a Hamilton cycle coincides with the hitting time for reaching minimum degree $2$. This resolves questions posed by Alon--Krivelevich in 2019 and by Frieze--Krivelevich in 2002. As a consequence, we determine the sharp threshold for Hamilton cycles in $(n,d,λ)$-graphs with $d/λ\ge C$ for all $d$ sufficiently large. Lastly, we extend our result to the minimum degree $2k$ versus $k$ edge-disjoint Hamilton cycles setting for $k \leq c\cdot \min\{d,\log n\}$ where $c$ is a constant depending on $C$. This advances on a question asked by Frieze.

title: Estimates of eigenvalues of elliptical differential problems in divergence form
generated_summary:
This paper establishes eigenvalue estimates for two classes of elliptic differential operators in divergence form on Riemannian manifolds: a coupled system of second-order equations and a fourth-order eigenvalue problem. The operators are defined using a symmetric positive definite tensor and a real-valued function, generalizing several well-known operators including the Laplacian, Cheng-Yau operator, drifted Laplacian, and biharmonic operator.

For the second-order coupled system on bounded domains in Euclidean space, the authors derive a universal quadratic inequality for eigenvalues extending Yang's classical estimate for the Laplacian. They also obtain bounds on sums of lower-order eigenvalues in terms of the first eigenvalue and its corresponding eigenfunction, subsequently applying the Cheng-Yang recursion formula to derive further inequalities. These results generalize previous work that was restricted to divergence-free tensors.

For the fourth-order problem on Riemannian manifolds isometrically immersed in Euclidean space, the authors prove eigenvalue inequalities involving the generalized mean curvature vector. A key improvement over prior results is that the new estimates yield a quadratic inequality in individual eigenvalues, enabling determination of gaps between consecutive eigenvalues—something previously unattainable in this generality. When specialized to the identity tensor and constant drifting function, the results recover known inequalities for the clamped plate problem established by Wang and Xia and by Cheng et al.

The significance of this work lies in providing a unified framework for eigenvalue estimation across a broad class of elliptic operators with applications in spectral theory, Riemannian geometry, and mathematical physics.
original_abstract: In this paper, we compute universal estimates of eigenvalues for a class of coupled systems of elliptic differential equations in divergence form on a bounded domain in Euclidean space, which includes the well-known Lamé and the Laplacian operator. Furthermore, we also give universal estimates of eigenvalues for a class of fourth-order elliptic differential problems in divergence form, which encloses the well-known bi-Laplacian operator. In both cases, as applications, we obtain the gap between consecutive eigenvalues as well as an upper bound for each eigenvalue.

title: Drift parameter estimation in the double mixed fractional Brownian model via solutions of Fredholm equations with singular kernels
generated_summary:
This paper addresses the practical computation of the maximum likelihood estimator (MLE) for the drift parameter in a double mixed fractional Brownian motion model, where the observed process is driven by the sum of two independent fractional Brownian motions with different Hurst parameters. While the MLE was previously established to be strongly consistent, L²-consistent, and finitely normal, it was not directly computable due to its dependence on the solution of an abstract operator equation lacking effective numerical procedures.

The main contribution is reformulating this operator equation as a Fredholm integral equation of the second kind with an explicitly characterized weakly singular kernel. The authors express this kernel in terms of hypergeometric functions and provide a detailed analysis of its singularities along the diagonal and near the boundary of the domain. This characterization enables the application of efficient numerical methods, specifically a modified product-integration method designed for weakly singular kernels.

A key advantage over alternative approaches is that the proposed estimator involves integration directly with respect to the observed process, avoiding nested integral transformations that introduce additional discretization errors. The numerical results demonstrate accurate approximation of the integral equation's solution and confirm the theoretical properties of the MLE through simulations, showing agreement between empirical and theoretical variances.

This work bridges the gap between the theoretical foundations of maximum likelihood estimation in mixed fractional models and their practical implementation, making these estimators accessible for applications in financial mathematics and other fields where multi-scale stochastic dynamics are modeled.
original_abstract: We consider drift parameter estimation in a model driven by the sum of two independent fractional Brownian motions with different Hurst indices. Although the maximum likelihood estimator (MLE) for this model is known theoretically, its computation requires solving an operator equation involving fractional covariance operators. We develop an effective numerical method for approximating the solution of this equation by reformulating it as a Fredholm integral equation of the second kind with a weakly singular kernel. The resulting algorithm enables practical computation of the MLE. Numerical experiments illustrate the performance of the method.

title: Computing Scaled Relative Graphs of Discrete-time LTI Systems from Data
generated_summary:
This paper extends the theory of Scaled Relative Graphs (SRGs) — a graphical tool for analyzing dynamical systems — from continuous-time to discrete-time linear time-invariant (LTI) systems, with particular emphasis on data-driven computation methods. Originally developed for convergence analysis of optimization algorithms, SRGs have shown promise in control theory for stability analysis, robustness assessment, and other applications.

The authors present three approaches for computing SRGs of discrete-time systems. First, when the state-space representation is known, the SRG can be obtained through linear matrix inequalities (LMIs) derived from the system's state-space matrices. Second, when the system is unknown but noise-free input-output data trajectories are available, the SRG can be computed exclusively from data, leveraging connections between SRGs and dissipativity theory. Third, for the practically important case of noisy data, the authors develop robust over-approximations of the SRG that are guaranteed to contain the true system's SRG.

The methodology connects state-space models to two types of operators defined over ℓ₂ spaces and their truncations, and exploits established relationships between dissipativity properties and data-driven analysis. The results build on prior work showing that dissipativity properties can be verified from data trajectories.

The significance of this work lies in enabling SRG-based graphical analysis for discrete-time systems without requiring explicit system models, thereby expanding the practical applicability of the SRG framework to data-driven control settings where model knowledge may be limited or unavailable.
original_abstract: Graphical methods for system analysis have played a central role in control theory. A recently emerging tool in this field is the Scaled Relative Graph (SRG). In this paper, we further extend its applicability by showing how the SRG of discrete-time linear-time-invariant (LTI) systems can be computed exactly from its state-space representation using linear matrix inequalities. We additionally propose a fully data-driven approach where we demonstrate how to compute the SRG exclusively from input-output data. Furthermore, we introduce a robust version of the SRG, which can be computed from noisy data trajectories and contains the SRG of the actual system.

title: 3d-3d correspondence and abelian flat connection
generated_summary:
This paper addresses a longstanding gap in the 3d-3d correspondence, which relates 3d complex Chern-Simons theory on a 3-manifold to 3d N=2 supersymmetric Chern-Simons matter theories. The central problem is that previous constructions of 3d N=2 theories from ideal tetrahedra decompositions failed to capture abelian flat connections, meaning they could not produce partition functions encompassing all flat connections, such as Jones polynomials.

The authors realize the homological block of knot complements for SU(2) gauge group—specifically in the form of the inverted Habiro series (the balanced expansion)—as a half-index of a 3d N=2 theory with particular boundary conditions and a specific choice of integration contour. The methodology involves working through explicit examples, primarily the figure-eight knot and trefoil knots, and then formulating general expectations for arbitrary knots. The key insight is that an appropriate choice of contour in the half-index computation naturally incorporates the abelian flat connection branch, with the contour passing through the critical point associated with this branch.

The main results include obtaining a 3d N=2 theory that captures all branches of flat connections, including the previously elusive abelian ones, and recovering the Jones polynomial by selecting a different set of poles. The authors also observe that the appearance of the abelian branch through contour choice appears specific to knot complements, where abelian flat connections are always present. This work represents significant progress toward constructing the full theory in the 3d-3d correspondence framework.
original_abstract: We realize a homological block of a knot complement in $S^3$ for $G_{\mathbb{C}}=SL(2,\mathbb{C})$ as a half-index of a 3d $\mathcal{N}=2$ theory via an expression of the homological block as an inverted Habiro series by working out some examples, which we expect to extend to general knots. Also, by choosing a certain set of poles in the integral expression of the half-index, we obtain the colored Jones polynomial.

title: Weighted Chui's conjecture
generated_summary:
This paper investigates a weighted generalization of Chui's conjecture, which posits that the average strength of an electrostatic field generated by unit charges on the unit circle is minimized when charges are uniformly distributed. The original conjecture remains open, though Newman established a lower bound for this quantity. The authors extend the problem in two directions: allowing non-uniform (but same-sign) charges of different magnitudes, and generalizing from the unit circle in the complex plane to the unit sphere in arbitrary dimension.

The main result establishes a Newman-type lower bound for the weighted case on the unit sphere in $\mathbb{R}^d$. Specifically, for positive weights $\alpha_k$ and points on the unit sphere, the authors prove that the integral of the squared magnitude of the weighted sum of Cauchy-type kernels over the unit ball is bounded below by a constant depending only on the dimension, multiplied by the square of the sum of weights. This result recovers Newman's classical bound when restricted to two dimensions with unit weights. The authors further demonstrate that their estimate is optimal when $d=2$ by constructing explicit configurations achieving the bound. They also show that the positivity assumption on the weights is essential, as signed weights can lead to arbitrarily small integrals.

The work connects to electrostatic theory, approximation by simplest fractions, and Cauchy transforms, providing a physically meaningful result: charges of the same sign on a sphere cannot fully compensate each other, ensuring a minimum average field strength.
original_abstract: The goals of this paper are threefold. First, we show that a counterpart of the Newman bound related to the Chui conjecture is valid in the case where the gradient of Coulomb potential is generated by arbitrary positive charges placed at the boundary of a unit ball. Second, we prove that our bound is sharp in the two-dimensional case. Finally, we discuss a related problem, where the unit charges are placed in the unit disc.

title: What induces plane structures in complete graph drawings?
generated_summary:
This paper investigates the fundamental conditions that force unavoidable plane structures in complete graph drawings in the plane. The main contribution is identifying the precise "breaking point" at which complete graph drawings must contain plane substructures, showing that the logical disjunction of two properties—adjacent-simplicity (adjacent edges cross at most once) and separate-simplicity (non-adjacent edges cross at most once)—is the critical threshold.

The authors prove that for any positive integer *k*, there exists a number *n* such that every complete graph drawing on *n* vertices satisfying either adjacent-simplicity or separate-simplicity must contain *k* pairwise disjoint edges. They complement this with a construction showing that without either condition, complete graph drawings on arbitrarily many vertices can exist where adjacent edges cross exactly once and non-adjacent edges cross between one and two times—avoiding disjoint edge pairs.

The paper further provides complete characterizations of guaranteed plane structures in each setting: for adjacent-simple drawings, these are exactly squids with isolated vertices and unions of disjoint caterpillars; for separate-simple drawings, these are exactly unions of disjoint edges and isolated vertices. The results extend to a physically motivated setting of stroke-like curves without the standard mild assumptions on drawings.

This work refines and improves earlier results by Pach and Tóth, precisely delineating the minimal crossing conditions that induce planarity phenomena. The characterization connects to classical concepts including stack and queue graphs, bridging topological graph theory with combinatorial structure.
original_abstract: This paper considers the task of connecting points on a piece of paper by drawing a curve between each pair of them. Under mild assumptions, we prove that many pairwise disjoint curves are unavoidable if either of the following rules is obeyed: any two adjacent curves do not cross, or any two non-adjacent curves cross at most once. Here, two curves are called adjacent if they share an endpoint. On the other hand, we demonstrate how to draw all curves such that any two adjacent curves cross exactly once, any two non-adjacent curves cross at least once and at most twice, and thus no two curves are disjoint. Furthermore, we analyze the emergence of disjoint curves without these mild assumptions, and characterize the plane structures in complete graph drawings guaranteed by each of the rules above.

title: Extending quasiconvex functions from uniformly convex sets
generated_summary:
This paper investigates the extendability of quasiconvex functions defined on convex bodies in finite-dimensional normed spaces, providing complete geometric characterizations of when such extensions are possible. Quasiconvex functions, whose sub-level sets are all convex, generalize convex functions but behave fundamentally differently regarding extension properties. Unlike convex Lipschitz functions, which always admit Lipschitz convex extensions via a simple formula, quasiconvex functions require specific geometric conditions on their domains for extension to the whole space.

The authors employ constructive techniques to demonstrate non-extendability under various conditions, building Lipschitz quasiconvex functions on convex bodies that cannot be extended to continuous or Lipschitz quasiconvex functions on the entire space. They establish that on every convex body in any normed space of dimension at least two, there exists a Lipschitz quasiconvex function admitting no Lipschitz quasiconvex extension. The paper further develops technical machinery for convex bodies without asymptotic directions to prove positive extension results preserving continuity, and treats upper semicontinuous quasiconvex functions separately.

The key achievement is obtaining exact finite-dimensional characterizations linking extendability of quasiconvex functions to geometric properties of the underlying convex body, particularly uniform rotundity and local uniform rotundity. These results clarify the sharp boundary between extendable and non-extendable cases, resolving the finite-dimensional aspects of a broader open problem about necessary geometric conditions for quasiconvex extension. The work has implications for optimization theory and mathematical programming, where quasiconvex functions are fundamental.
original_abstract: Let $X$ be a normed space of a finite dimension at least two, and $C\subsetneq X$ a closed convex set with nonempty interior. We are interested in extending Lipschitz quasiconvex functions on $C$ to quasiconvex functions on $X$. We show that, unlike what holds for convex functions, in general one cannot obtain Lipschitz extensions (except for trivial cases). If we require just uniformly continuous or continuous extensions, such extendability properties for $C$ are shown to be characterized by some geometric properties of $C$.

title: Optimization with Parametric Variational Inequality Constraints on a Moving Set
generated_summary:
This paper addresses optimization problems with parametric variational inequality (PVI) constraints defined on a moving set, where the feasible region evolves with the problem's parameters. Unlike most existing work on mathematical programs with equilibrium constraints (MPEC), which assumes a fixed constraint set for the variational inequality, this work tackles the more general and practically relevant case where the constraint set depends on upper-level decision variables—a setting that arises in machine learning hyperparameter tuning, portfolio optimization, and traffic network design.

The authors first establish that the PVI solution function is Lipschitz continuous with respect to the upper-level decision variable and that the optimal solution set is nonempty and bounded. A notable theoretical contribution is demonstrating that metric regularity of the constraint system holds automatically, enabling stationary point characterization without additional constraint qualifications. To address the nonsmoothness introduced by the projection operator onto a moving set, the authors extend smoothing approximation techniques from fixed-set variational inequalities to the parametric setting. They establish consistency between the original and smoothed problems and propose a Smoothing Implicit Gradient Algorithm (SIGA) that leverages the implicit function theorem with a gradually diminishing smoothing parameter.

The authors prove that any accumulation point of the sequence generated by SIGA converges to a stationary point of the original problem. Numerical experiments on portfolio management problems with real data validate SIGA's effectiveness, demonstrating its practical applicability to problems where constraint sets shift dynamically with decision variables.
original_abstract: This paper focuses on optimization problems constrained by Parametric Variational Inequalities (PVI) defined on a moving set. Unlike most existing works on mathematical programs with equilibrium constraints, the equilibrium constraints have parameters not only in the function but also in the related set. We show that the solution function of the PVI is Lipschitz continuous with respect to the upper-level decision variables and the solution set of the optimization problem is nonempty and bounded. Moreover, we prove that the metric regularity of the constraints holds automatically, which allow us to characterize stationary points without any additional assumptions. A Smoothing Implicit Gradient Algorithm (SIGA) is proposed based on the smoothing approximation of the PVI. We prove the convergence of SIGA to a stationary point of the optimization problem and numerically validate the efficiency of SIGA by portfolio management problems with real data.

title: An efficient and accurate numerical method for computing the ground states of three-dimensional rotating dipolar Bose-Einstein condensates under strongly anisotropic trap
generated_summary:
This paper presents an efficient and accurate numerical method for computing ground states of three-dimensional rotating dipolar Bose-Einstein condensates (BEC) under strongly anisotropic trapping potentials. The main contribution is the integration of the anisotropic truncated kernel method (ATKM) with a preconditioned conjugate gradient (PCG) optimization algorithm, specifically designed to overcome three key challenges: the vastly different spatial scales introduced by anisotropic traps, the singular and nonlocal dipolar interaction kernel, and the complex energy landscape created by fast rotation.

The methodology combines Fourier spectral discretization on anisotropic rectangular domains with ATKM for evaluating the dipolar potential, achieving spectral accuracy with FFT-like efficiency. Crucially, unlike previous approaches such as the kernel truncation method or nonuniform FFT, the memory requirements of ATKM are independent of the anisotropy strength, making the method practical for strongly anisotropic regimes. The PCG framework, equipped with an appropriate step size control strategy, accelerates convergence compared to traditional imaginary-time evolution methods.

Key results include extensive numerical validation of accuracy and efficiency, identification of novel ground state patterns, observation of bent (U-shaped) vortex lines in dipolar BEC, and comprehensive investigations of how model parameters affect critical rotational frequency, energies, and chemical potential. The significance of this work lies in enabling practical three-dimensional simulations of strongly anisotropic dipolar BEC systems where low-dimensional approximations are inadequate, particularly for studying vortex structures that exist only in three dimensions.
original_abstract: In this article, we propose an efficient and spectrally accurate numerical method to compute the ground states of three-dimensional (3D) rotating dipolar Bose-Einstein condensates (BEC) under strongly anisotropic trapping potentials.The kernel singularity, convolution non-locality and density anisotropy together complicate the dipolar potential evaluation. The fast rotation mechanism not only induces a complicated energy landscape with many local minima, but also creates a large number of vortices in the condensates. Such factors collectively make the ground state computation challenging in terms of convergence, accuracy and efficiency, especially for 3D anisotropic systems. Coupled with Fourier spectral discretization, we proposed a preconditioned conjugate gradient method (PCG) by integrating the anisotropic truncated kernel method (ATKM) for the dipolar potential evaluation. An adaptive step size control strategy is designed and ATKM allows for a spectral accuracy without introducing any extra anisotropy-dependent memory requirement or computational time. Our algorithm is spectrally accurate, highly efficient and memory-economic. Extensive numerical results are presented to confirm the accuracy and efficiency, together with applications to study impacts of the model parameters on critical rotational frequency, energies and chemical potential. Furthermore, these simulations reveal additional novel ground state patterns, such as bent vortices.

title: Regularization of the superposition principle: Potential theory meets Fokker-Planck equations
generated_summary:
This paper addresses a fundamental open problem in the theory of Fokker-Planck equations and stochastic differential equations: whether the Markov processes obtained through the superposition principle possess the strong Markov property, rather than merely the simple Markov property previously established.

The authors construct right (hence strong Markov) processes associated with solutions to both linear and nonlinear time-dependent Fokker-Planck equations. Their methodology combines three distinct mathematical frameworks: the theory of generalized Dirichlet forms for time-dependent operators, the classical superposition principle connecting Fokker-Planck equations to martingale problems, and probabilistic potential theory. The construction proceeds in three stages: first building local right processes on finite time intervals using generalized Dirichlet forms, then forming a global process via projective limits under a restricted uniqueness assumption, and finally extending this process to a conservative right process with continuous paths on a full-measure subset of the state space.

Key results include the construction of fundamental flow solutions to linear Fokker-Planck equations, solutions to backward Kolmogorov and parabolic Dirichlet problems via hitting distributions, maximal tail estimates through Lyapunov functions, and the construction of Choquet capacities for nonlinear Fokker-Planck equations. The theory extends to McKean-Vlasov SDEs, establishing strong Markov properties for their weak solutions. The authors demonstrate applicability to generalized porous media equations, providing explicit sufficient conditions on coefficients. These results significantly advance the probabilistic analysis of PDEs with merely measurable coefficients.
original_abstract: For a solution to a (possibly nonlinear) Fokker-Planck equation (FPE) the powerful superposition principle renders a probability measure on path space with one dimensional time marginals equal to this solution, and additionally solving the martingale problem for the Kolmogorov operator given by the FPE. The superposition principle thus reveals that such parabolic PDEs have a probabilistic counter part. The aim of this work is to go a substantial further step and, by exploiting the superposition principle, construct a full fledged Markov process, i.e. a family of path space measures for a large set of space time starting points connected by the Markov property, associated to the (linearized) FPE in the above way. Under very general (merely measurability) conditions on the coefficients of the FPE this is achieved in this paper in such a way that the resulting process is a right process, which is a particularly useful class of Markov processes, enjoying among other regularity properties the strong Markov property, which is fundamental for the analysis of the underlying FPE as a (nonlinear) parabolic PDE by probabilistic tools. As two main applications we construct fundamental flow solutions for the FPE and we prove a well-posedeness result for the parabolic Dirichlet problem through probabilistic means for more general coefficients than could be treated in the existing literature. Furthermore, we introduce a Choquet capacity for such FPEs using the corresponding right process. The validity of the strong Markov property in the context of the superposition principle was an open problem even in the linear case. In this paper we solve this also in the nonlinear case, i.e. for path laws of solutions to McKean-Vlasov SDEs with Nemytskii type coefficients. A main application here is the FPE given by the generalized porous media equation and its corresponding McKean-Vlasov SDE.

title: Complete Nevanlinna-Pick property of $\mathbb K$-Invariant Reproducing Kernels
generated_summary:
This paper investigates the complete Nevanlinna-Pick (CNP) property for K-invariant reproducing kernels defined on irreducible Cartan domains, which generalize the open unit disc and Euclidean unit ball to higher-rank settings. The main contribution is extending the theory of CNP kernels and their associated operator-theoretic machinery from the well-studied ball setting to the broader class of Cartan domains.

The authors employ the Peter-Weyl decomposition of polynomial spaces under the action of the maximal compact subgroup K, expressing K-invariant kernels as sums over signatures indexed by partitions. They derive a factorization of the reciprocal kernel analogous to the classical one-variable case, obtaining a sequence of real numbers that governs the CNP property. By generalizing the Kaluza lemma to this multi-variable signature setting, they establish necessary conditions for an irreducible K-invariant kernel to possess the CNP property in terms of its coefficients.

Key results include a characterization of K-invariant CNP kernels on Cartan domains through the existence of characteristic functions for K-contractions — commuting operator tuples satisfying a positivity condition determined by the kernel. For kernels possessing the CNP property, the authors provide an explicit construction of the characteristic function and prove that it serves as a complete unitary invariant for pure K-contractions, extending the classical Sz.-Nagy–Foias theory.

This work significantly broadens the scope of Nevanlinna-Pick interpolation theory and model theory for operator tuples to the rich geometric setting of Cartan domains.
original_abstract: Let $Ω$ be a Cartan domain and $K = \sum_{\underline s}a_{\underline s}K_{\underline s}$ be a $\mathbb K$-invariant kernel on $Ω$. In this article, we first obtain a necessary condition on $K$ to have the complete Nevanlinna-Pick property in terms of the sequence $\{a_{\underline s}\}_{\underline s}$ with the assumption that each $a_{\underline s}$ is non-zero and $K$ is non-vanishing. This generalizes the well-known Kaluza's Lemma in the context of $\mathbb K$-invariant kernels.
