Since the period functions of the surface family are annihilated by the Jordan-Pochhammer operator, the computed functions generate a subgroup of appropriate rank in holomorphic functions modulo periods.

The significance lies in extending regulator computations and indecomposability results to a substantially more general class of surfaces, connecting higher algebraic K-theory with Appell-Lauricella hypergeometric functions and Jordan-Pochhammer differential equations, though the generality comes at the cost of slightly weaker bounds in the previously studied special case.
original_abstract: In this paper, we construct higher Chow cycles of type $(2, 1)$ on a family of surfaces related to a product of curves, which are certain degree $N$ abelian covers of $\mathbb{P}^1$ branched over $n+2$ points. We prove that for a very general member, these cycles generate a subgroup of the indecomposable part of $\operatorname{rank} \ge n\cdot \varphi(N)$, where $\varphi(N)$ is Euler's totient function, by computing their images under the transcendental regulator map.

title: A class of stochastic control problems with state constraints
generated_summary:
This paper addresses linear-quadratic stochastic control problems where a diffusion process must be steered to remain within a constrained region of the state space while minimizing an expected cost that depends on the state and is quadratic in the control effort. Such problems arise naturally in applications like optimal vehicle navigation, where collisions with obstacles must be avoided.

The authors adopt a purely probabilistic approach, leveraging logarithmic transformations, diffusion theory, and Itô calculus, in contrast to prior work relying on PDE methods or backward stochastic differential equations. A key contribution is the closed-form expression for the value function, which is shown to equal the negative logarithm of the expected exponential payoff of an unconstrained process killed upon exiting the admissible domain. The value function is proven to be continuously differentiable in time and twice continuously differentiable in space within the interior of the constraint set, and it solves a Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation with singular boundary conditions.

The authors construct an optimal Markovian control in strong form, adapted to the Brownian filtration, despite the control blowing up at the domain boundary. The framework substantially relaxes regularity assumptions on the domain boundary compared to earlier work, requiring only "regularity in the sense of diffusions" rather than smooth boundaries. The probabilistic representation enables explicit solutions when the killed process density is known and facilitates Monte Carlo simulation otherwise. The results generalize classical connections to risk-sensitive optimization and Doob's h-transform as special cases.
original_abstract: We obtain a probabilistic solution to linear-quadratic optimal control problems with state constraints. Given a closed set $\mathcal{D}\subseteq [0,T]\times\mathbb{R}^d$, a diffusion $X$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$ must be linearly controlled in order to keep the time-space process $(t,X_t)$ inside the set $\mathcal{C}:=([0,T]\times\mathbb{R}^d)\setminus\mathcal{D}$, while at the same time minimising an expected cost that depends on the state $(t,X_t)$ and is quadratic in the speed of the control exerted. We find a probabilistic representation for the value function and an optimal control under a set of mild sufficient conditions concerning the coefficients of the underlying dynamics and the regularity of the set $\mathcal{D}$. The optimally controlled dynamics is in strong form, in the sense that it is adapted to the filtration generated by the driving Brownian motion. Fully explicit formulae are presented in some relevant examples.

title: Lattice points arising from regularity and $\mathrm{v}$-number of Graphs: Whisker and Cameron-Walker
generated_summary:
This paper investigates the lattice points arising as pairs of Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity and v-number (Vasconcelos number) for edge ideals of connected graphs on a fixed number of vertices. Since no general relationship exists between these two invariants—each can be arbitrarily larger than the other—determining which pairs are achievable represents a fundamental combinatorial and algebraic challenge.

The authors first establish an upper bound for the v-number using the edge domination number of a graph. They then identify two explicit subsets of achievable lattice points for general connected graphs on n vertices, showing that for n ≥ 7, these pairs include specific regions characterized by regularity and v-number constraints involving tree and chordal graph constructions.

The paper's central contributions are complete characterizations of achievable (regularity, v-number) pairs for two important graph classes. For connected whisker graphs on 2m vertices, the lattice points form the set of pairs (r, v) where 1 ≤ v ≤ r ≤ m. For Cameron-Walker graphs on n vertices, the authors provide a precise description that depends on whether n ≤ 6 or n ≥ 7, yielding a more complex but fully determined region of achievable pairs.

The methodology combines explicit graph constructions to realize specific invariant pairs with algebraic arguments bounding the invariants. This work initiates a systematic study of v-number behavior across graph families and concludes with a conjecture for chordal graphs, suggesting directions for future research in this emerging area connecting coding theory, commutative algebra, and combinatorics.
original_abstract: Let $G$ be a simple graph on $n$ vertices and $I(G)\subseteq R$ be its edge ideal. In this paper, we initiate the study of determining lattice points in $\mathbb{N}^2$ that appear as a pair $(\mathrm{reg}(R/I(G)), \mathrm{v}(I(G)))$, where $G$ ranges over all connected graphs on $n$ vertices, and we denote this set by $\mathcal{RV}(n)$. Here `$\mathrm{reg}$' denotes the (Castelnuovo-Mumford) regularity and `$\mathrm{v}$' denotes the $\mathrm{v}$-number. We establish general bounds for $\mathcal{RV}(n)$ by identifying two sets $A(n)$ and $B(n)$ satisfying $A(n)\subseteq \mathcal{RV}(n)\subseteq B(n)$. Furthermore, we explicitly determine the subsets of $\mathcal{RV}(n)$ consisting of all possible pairs $(\mathrm{reg}(R/I(G)), \mathrm{v}(I(G)))$ arising from whisker graphs and Cameron-Walker graphs on $n$ vertices. Finally, we propose a conjecture on the subset of $\mathcal{RV}(n)$ arising from connected chordal graphs.

title: Transformations and functions that preserve the asymptotic mean of digits in the ternary representation of a number

The authors build upon their earlier introduction of this concept and its connections to digit frequencies and fractal set theory.

The main contribution is the identification and systematic study of functions that act as invariants of the asymptotic mean of digits, operating both everywhere and almost everywhere (in the Lebesgue measure sense) on the unit interval. The paper also examines functions that preserve individual digit frequencies in the *s*-adic representation. The methodology relies on the symbolic dynamics framework of *s*-adic representations, leveraging the relationship between digit frequencies and the asymptotic mean — specifically, that when all digit frequencies exist, the asymptotic mean equals the weighted sum of digits multiplied by their respective frequencies.

The work is situated within a rich tradition connecting number representation theory to metric number theory, ergodic theory, and fractal analysis. The paper draws on classical results including Borel's theorem on normal numbers and the Hausdorff-Besicovitch dimension formula for Besicovitch-Eggleston sets. The significance lies in providing a new lens for understanding structural properties of real numbers through digit-based invariants, with potential applications to the study of singular functions, probability distributions, and fractal geometry.
original_abstract: In the paper we study transformations of the interval $[0;1)$ and functions that preserve the asymptotic mean $r$ of the digits in the $s$--adic representation of a number $x$, $$r(x)=\lim\limits_{n\to\infty}\frac{1}{n}\sum\limits^{n}_{i=1}α_i(x)$$ specify the necessary and sufficient conditions for a transformation to belong to this class

title: Stability conditions on noncommutative crepant resolutions of 3-dimensional isolated singularities
generated_summary:
This paper studies Bridgeland stability conditions on derived categories of finite-length modules over maximal modification algebras (MMAs) associated with three-dimensional complete local Gorenstein isolated singularities. MMAs serve as noncommutative analogs of minimal models in algebraic geometry, and understanding their derived categories bridges Cohen–Macaulay representation theory and birational geometry.

The authors generalize previous work restricted to terminal singularities by constructing a wall-and-chamber structure in the real Grothendieck group, where chambers correspond to modifying modules obtained through iterated mutations. They introduce the notion of descending paths to characterize minimal-length paths between modifying modules and develop a groupoid action from this combinatorial structure. A key technical advance involves lifting mutation functors to quasi-functors of dg-categories, enabling a criterion for compositions of mutation functors to be identity functors in the general isolated singularity setting.

The main result establishes that the subspace of modifying stability conditions forms a full-dimensional, path-connected subspace admitting a regular covering map to a complexified mutation cone, with the Galois group generated by mutation functors. This yields a fundamental group action on the derived category and a complete description of the autoequivalence group preserving modifying stability conditions, extending previous results for terminal singularities. The authors also prove that modification algebras over isolated singularities are locally tilting-noetherian and locally tilting-artinian, and they conjecture a global tilting-noetherian property equivalent to a noncommutative analog of Kawamata's connectedness theorem for minimal models.
original_abstract: Let $R$ be a 3-dimensional complete local Gorenstein isolated singularity. For a basic maximal modifying $R$-module $M$, we construct a wall-and-chamber structure, denoted by ${\sf Cone}(M)$ and called the mutation cone of $M$, in the real Grothendieck group associated to the maximal modification algebra $Λ={\rm End}_R(M)$. Each chamber in ${\sf Cone}(M)$ corresponds to a maximal modifying module obtained by iterated (Iyama--Wemyss) mutations of $M$, and a wall-crossing corresponds to the mutation at an indecomposable summand. Moreover, we introduce the notion of tilting-noetherian property of $Λ$, and by analysis of wall-and-chamber structure of ${\sf Cone}(M)$, we prove that this property holds for $Λ$ if and only if all maximal modifying $R$-modules are connected by iterated mutations.   We then consider the finite length subcategory $\mathscr{D}_M\subset {\rm D}^{\rm b}({\rm mod}\,Λ)$ and introduce a full-dimensional connected subspace ${\rm Stab}^{\rm mdf}\mathscr{D}_M\subset{\rm Stab}\mathscr{D}_M$ of Bridgeland stability conditions on $\mathscr{D}_M$. We prove that there is a regular covering map from ${\rm Stab}^{\rm mdf}\mathscr{D}_M$ to the complexification ${\sf Cone}(M)_{\mathbb{C}}$ of the mutation cone of $M$, where the Galois group is the subgroup of ${\rm Auteq} \mathscr{D}_M$ consisting of compositions of equivalences associated to mutations of maximal modifying modules. Finally, using the results on stability conditions, we describe the group of autoequivalences of $\mathscr{D}_M$ that preserve the subspace ${\rm Stab}^{\rm mdf}\mathscr{D}_M$.

title: Policy Optimization of Mixed H2/H-infinity Control: Benign Nonconvexity and Global Optimality

A key technical contribution is the construction of a novel convex lifting for two-channel mixed control that employs non-strict Riccati inequalities, departing from the classical approach based on strict inequalities. This distinction enables certification of global optimality over the entire feasible set, including boundary policies.

The main results establish several fundamental properties. The feasible set is open and path-connected, with its boundary precisely characterized by policies saturating the H-infinity constraint. The cost function is real analytic in the interior and continuous on the closure of its domain. Most notably, the authors prove that every stationary point of the nonconvex problem is globally optimal, demonstrating the absence of spurious stationary points. original_abstract: Mixed H2/H-infinity control balances performance and robustness by minimizing an H2 cost bound subject to an H-infinity constraint. However, classical Riccati/LMI solutions offer limited insight into the nonconvex optimization landscape and do not readily scale to large-scale or data-driven settings. In this paper, we revisit mixed H2/H-infinity control from a modern policy optimization viewpoint, including the general two-channel and single-channel cases. One central result is that both cases enjoy a benign nonconvex structure: every stationary point is globally optimal. We characterize the H-infinity-constrained feasible set, which is open, path-connected, with boundary given exactly by policies saturating the H-infinity constraint. We also show that the mixed objective is real analytic in the interior with explicit gradient formulas. Our key analysis builds on an Extended Convex Lifting (ECL) framework that bridges nonconvex policy optimization and convex reformulations. The ECL constructions rely on non-strict Riccati inequalities that allow us to characterize global optimality. These insights reveal hidden convexity in mixed H2/H-infinity control and facilitate the design of scalable policy iteration methods in large-scale settings.

title: Bergman kernels and Poincaré series

These tools enable the authors to prove absolute and uniform convergence of the averaging series on compact subsets.

The key results include the convergence theorem for Bergman kernels (Theorem 1.1) and its application to relative Poincaré series, where holomorphic sections invariant under a full discrete group are constructed from sections invariant under a subgroup by averaging over cosets. Using asymptotic expansions of isotropic states associated with Bohr-Sommerfeld submanifolds, the authors prove non-vanishing of these relative Poincaré series for sufficiently large weight. Specific applications are given for discrete subgroups acting on the hyperbolic plane and the unit ball in higher dimensions, involving closed geodesics generated by hyperbolic and loxodromic elements.

The significance lies in unifying Bergman kernel theory with classical automorphic forms, extending previous results from smooth compact quotients to the broader setting of finite-volume orbifolds with bounded geometry.
original_abstract: We show that the Bergman kernel of a finite-volume quotient of a Hermitian manifold $\widetilde{X}$ with bounded geometry by a discrete group $Γ$ of its isometries is the same as the averaging over $Γ$ of the Bergman kernel on $\widetilde{X}$. We then use these results when $\widetilde{X}$ is a Hermitian symmetric space to show that a large class of relative Poincaré series does not vanish. This extends the results of Borthwick-Paul-Uribe and Barron (formerly Foth) to the case of general locally symmetric spaces of finite volume.

title: The Hochschild cohomlogy ring of a self-injective Nakayama algebra is a Batalin-Vilkoviskys algebra
generated_summary:

While prior work established that Frobenius algebras with semisimple Nakayama automorphisms possess BV structures, the question posed by Lambre, Zhou, and Zimmermann—whether this extends to nonsemisimple Nakayama automorphisms—remained open, with a recent counterexample showing the answer is negative in general.

The authors employ a computational approach, systematically reviewing and correcting existing results on Hochschild cohomology of truncated basic cycle algebras, including cohomology spaces, cup product formulas, ring presentations, and Gerstenhaber brackets. The main result establishes that the Hochschild cohomology ring of any truncated basic cycle algebra over a field carries a BV algebra structure, regardless of whether the Nakayama automorphism is semisimple. This affirmatively answers the Lambre-Zhou-Zimmermann question for the important class of self-injective Nakayama algebras, and the general criterion developed for constructing BV operators in the nonsemisimple case may have independent interest for studying other algebra classes.
original_abstract: Lambre, Zhou and Zimmermann showed that the Hochschild cohomology ring of a Frobenius algebra with semisimple Nakayama automorphism is a Batalin-Vilkovisky algebra. They asked whether the semisimplicity condition is necessary. In this paper, we show that for a self-injective Nakayama algebra, the Hochschild cohomology ring is always a Batalin-Vilkovisky algebra.   In course of proofs, we correct some inaccuracies in the literature, hoping not to introduce new errors.

title: BBP Phase Transition for a Doubly Sparse Deformed Model
generated_summary:

The key result confirms a sharp phase transition: below a critical signal-to-noise threshold (which depends on both sparsity parameters), the leading eigenvalue remains within the bulk and the eigenvector carries no information about the spike; above the threshold, the eigenvalue separates from the bulk and the leading eigenvector achieves non-trivial correlation with the true signal. Notably, the recovery result applies to multiple overlapping spike vectors without requiring orthogonal invariance of the noise.

The work is significant for connecting sparse PCA, the planted clique problem, and robust PCA within a unified spectral framework, extending BBP theory to practically relevant doubly sparse settings.
original_abstract: We prove the equivalent of the Baik, Ben Arous, Péché (2004) phenomenon for a novel, doubly sparse model where both the Wigner noise matrix and signal vector(s) are sparse. Specifically, we consider a deformed sub-Gaussian sparse Wigner ensemble with a fixed number of sub-Gaussian spike vectors of the same-order sparsity added. We show that spike vectors with signals greater than one are correlated with the top eigenvectors of the deformed ensemble and that each spike vector of signal greater than one induces an outlier eigenvalue. Notably, our results hold in the supercritical sparsity regime for the Wigner matrix ($q \gg \frac{\log n}{n}$) and for any sparse spike vector with an unbounded number of entries ($np\to \infty$). No further relationship between the sparsities of the noise matrix ($q$) and spike vectors ($p$) is necessary. This generalizes the work of Benaych-Georges and Nadakuditi (2010) and Péché (2005).

title: Multilevel Training for Kolmogorov Arnold Networks
generated_summary:
This paper establishes a theoretical and algorithmic framework for multilevel training of Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KANs), demonstrating that multigrid-inspired methods can achieve significant algorithmic speedups in neural network training. This equivalence yields a faster non-recursive implementation of spline-based KANs compared to standard Cox-de Boor recursion.

Building on this insight, the authors introduce the concept of *properly nested hierarchies* for multilevel optimization, ensuring that interpolation from coarse to fine models preserves approximation progress. Combined with the complementary relaxation properties inherent to the spline basis across hierarchy levels, this framework satisfies the key requirements for effective multigrid methods.

Numerical experiments on functional regression and physics-informed neural networks demonstrate 2–3 orders of magnitude improvement in accuracy compared to standard training and comparable MLPs. Notably, multilevel training under the equivalent ReLU basis provides essentially no improvement, confirming that both proper nesting and complementary optimization dynamics are essential. This work represents a principled demonstration that multigrid principles can deliver substantial efficiency gains in neural network training when paired with appropriately structured architectures.
original_abstract: Algorithmic speedup of training common neural architectures is made difficult by the lack of structure guaranteed by the function compositions inherent to such networks. In contrast to multilayer perceptrons (MLPs), Kolmogorov-Arnold networks (KANs) provide more structure by expanding learned activations in a specified basis. This paper exploits this structure to develop practical algorithms and theoretical insights, yielding training speedup via multilevel training for KANs. To do so, we first establish an equivalence between KANs with spline basis functions and multichannel MLPs with power ReLU activations through a linear change of basis. We then analyze how this change of basis affects the geometry of gradient-based optimization with respect to spline knots. The KANs change-of-basis motivates a multilevel training approach, where we train a sequence of KANs naturally defined through a uniform refinement of spline knots with analytic geometric interpolation operators between models. The interpolation scheme enables a ``properly nested hierarchy'' of architectures, ensuring that interpolation to a fine model preserves the progress made on coarse models, while the compact support of spline basis functions ensures complementary optimization on subsequent levels. Numerical experiments demonstrate that our multilevel training approach can achieve orders of magnitude improvement in accuracy over conventional methods to train comparable KANs or MLPs, particularly for physics informed neural networks. Finally, this work demonstrates how principled design of neural networks can lead to exploitable structure, and in this case, multilevel algorithms that can dramatically improve training performance.

title: The Archimedean height pairing for differential forms on degeneration of Riemann surfaces
generated_summary:

The main contribution is proving that for two smooth real (1,1)-forms that are cohomologically trivial on smooth fibers of a one-parameter degeneration, their Archimedean height pairing extends continuously to the singular fiber after subtracting a logarithmic correction term determined by the intersection matrix of irreducible components of the singular fiber via its Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse.

The methodology relies on introducing "preferred potentials" for the differential forms and deriving asymptotic estimates using work of Dai and Yoshikawa on eigenfunctions with small eigenvalues on degenerating Riemann surfaces, combined with continuity results for fiber integrals near singular fibers.

The key application concerns parabolic dynamics on projective elliptic K3 surfaces. The author proves that the current-valued pairing introduced by Filip and Tosatti has a continuous potential for a finite index subgroup of fiber-preserving automorphisms, removing their earlier assumption that singular fibers be reduced and irreducible. This yields that limit currents arising from iterations of parabolic automorphisms have continuous potentials. Additionally, the author shows that convergence of these currents cannot occur in the C¹ topology, providing a counterexample to a question posed by Tosatti regarding convergence regularity for Ricci-flat metrics.
original_abstract: We define the Archimedean height pairing for fiberwise cohomologically trivial differential forms on a one-parameter degeneration of Riemann surfaces, and we study its asymptotic behavior. The proof relies on recent work by Dai--Yoshikawa on the asymptotics of small eigenvalues. As an application, we relate this pairing to the current-valued pairing of Filip--Tosatti, extending their construction to broader geometric settings.

title: The Conjugacy Relation on One-sided Subshifts is Non-treeable
generated_summary:

While the complexity of conjugacy relations on two-sided subshifts is well-understood—Clemens showed it is Borel bireducible with the universal countable Borel equivalence relation—the one-sided case has remained largely unexplored.

The main contribution is establishing that the conjugacy relation on transitive one-sided subshifts over the binary alphabet {0,1} is a non-treeable and non-amenable countable Borel equivalence relation. This partially answers Clemens's open question about the complexity of one-sided shift isomorphism. The authors build upon earlier work by Deka, Kwietniak, Peng, and Sabok, who proved analogous results for subshifts with the specification property. While the two-sided case techniques can yield non-treeability for one-sided subshifts with sufficiently large alphabets, shrinking the alphabet to just two symbols requires nontrivial modifications to existing constructions.

The methodology involves adapting constructions from the two-sided setting to the one-sided context, overcoming technical challenges that arise because one-sided subshifts lack invertibility. The significance of this result lies in demonstrating that even with the smallest nontrivial alphabet, the conjugacy relation on one-sided subshifts already exhibits high complexity, being strictly more complex than hyperfinite equivalence relations. This places important constraints on any potential classification scheme for one-sided dynamical systems.
original_abstract: In this paper we study the conjugacy relation on one-sided subshifts in the viewpoint of descriptive set theory. We show the conjugacy relation on one sided subshifts with the alphabet set $\{0,1\}$ is non-treeable and non-amenable.

title: The minimum length of an axis-aligned rectangular tiling of a flat torus
generated_summary:
This paper investigates an optimization problem concerning axis-aligned rectangular tilings of flat tori, seeking to determine the minimum total length of line segments needed to partition a flat torus into axis-aligned rectangles. A flat torus is defined as the quotient of the Euclidean plane over a lattice generated by a given basis, and the rectangles in the tiling must have sides aligned with the coordinate axes.

The main contribution is a closed-form formula for this minimum length, expressed in terms of the lattice basis that defines the flat torus. The authors demonstrate that optimal tilings are remarkably simple in structure, requiring either exactly one or exactly two rectangles to achieve the minimum total perimeter. When two rectangles are used, the paper identifies two possible geometric configurations for the tiling arrangement.

The methodology involves analyzing the geometric constraints imposed by the lattice structure on axis-aligned rectangular partitions, determining how the choice of basis affects the achievable total edge length, and constructing explicit optimal tilings. The length metric is defined as half the sum of all rectangle perimeters, since each internal edge is shared by adjacent rectangles.

This work connects to several established research areas, including rectangular subdivisions in discrete geometry, VLSI floorplanning, orthogonal graph drawing, and toroidal graph representations. The result extends the classical study of rectangulations to the toroidal setting and contributes to the broader understanding of optimization problems for rectangular partitions on non-planar surfaces, providing an elegant characterization of optimal solutions with minimal combinatorial complexity.
original_abstract: A flat torus is the quotient of the Euclidean plane over a lattice generated by a basis, and an axis-aligned rectangular tiling of a flat torus is a partition into finitely many rectangles whose sides are axis-aligned. We provide the minimum sum of the perimeter of rectangles for an axis-aligned rectangular tiling, and prove that it is attainable by either exactly one rectangle or exactly two rectangles.

title: Robust estimation via $γ$-divergence for diffusion processes
generated_summary:
This paper proposes robust estimation methods for discretely observed diffusion processes using two divergence-based approaches: the density power divergence and the γ-divergence. The work addresses the well-known vulnerability of likelihood-based estimators to outliers in high-frequency observation data from diffusion processes, which are widely used in physics, biology, finance, and engineering.

The authors construct minimum contrast estimators based on both divergences by utilizing the quasi-likelihood framework for discretely observed diffusion processes. They establish the asymptotic properties of the proposed estimators, proving both consistency and asymptotic normality under standard regularity conditions. A central contribution is the rigorous analysis of robustness properties through conditional influence functions. The authors demonstrate that both divergence-based estimators possess bounded influence functions and exhibit redescending properties, meaning their influence on parameter estimates decreases for extreme outlying observations—a desirable robustness characteristic that the standard quasi-maximum likelihood estimator lacks.

Monte Carlo simulations are conducted under several contamination models, including additive outliers and replacement outliers, comparing the divergence-based estimators against likelihood-based estimation. The numerical results confirm that the proposed estimators maintain substantially lower bias and mean squared error in the presence of outliers while maintaining competitive efficiency under clean data conditions.

The significance of this work lies in providing theoretically grounded and practically effective robust alternatives to quasi-maximum likelihood estimation for diffusion processes, with the γ-divergence-based estimator offering particularly strong robustness guarantees through its redescending influence function properties.
original_abstract: This paper deals with the problem of outliers in high frequency observation data from diffusion processes. Robust estimation methods are needed because the inclusion of outliers can lead to incorrect statistical inference even in the diffusion process. To construct a robust estimator, we first approximate the transition density of the diffusion process to the Gaussian density by using Kessler's approach and then employ two types of minimum robust divergence estimation methods. In this paper, we provide the asymptotic properties of the robust estimator using $γ$-divergence. Furthermore, we derive the conditional influence functions of the estimation using divergences and discuss its boundness.

title: Cotype of random polytopes
generated_summary:
This paper establishes dimension-independent cotype bounds for normed spaces generated by random Gaussian polytopes, addressing fundamental questions in high-dimensional convex geometry and Banach space theory. The main contribution is proving that for a symmetric random polytope generated by i.i.d. standard Gaussian vectors in n-dimensional space, the associated normed space has finite cotype with constants independent of dimension, provided the number of generating vectors satisfies certain proportionality conditions relative to the dimension.

The methodology combines techniques from high-dimensional probability, geometric functional analysis, and convex geometry. The proof involves multiple reduction steps: analyzing potential low-distortion embeddings of ℓ∞ spaces into sections of the random polytope, establishing incompressibility properties of coefficient vectors, developing a novel net argument on Grassmannians using an operator-valued geometric series expansion for orthogonal projections, and treating separately cases where embedding vectors have comparable or disparate ℓ₁ and ℓ∞ norms.

The key results are twofold. First, any k-dimensional section of the Gaussian polytope is at polynomial (in k) Banach–Mazur distance from the ℓ∞ space. Second, applying the Maurey–Pisier theorem, this yields the desired cotype bounds. As a significant application, the authors construct a separable Banach space of finite cotype with maximal local inhomogeneity, demonstrating that infinite cotype is not necessary for extremal behavior of the subspace inhomogeneity functional—answering a natural question in Banach space geometry.
original_abstract: For $N\geq n$, let $P_{N,n}$ be a random polytope in ${\mathbb R}^n$ with vertices $\pm X_i$, $1\leq i\leq N$, where $X_1,\dots,X_N$ are i.i.d standard Gaussian vectors in ${\mathbb R}^n$. Random polytopes $P_{N,n}$, as well as their duals, are classical objects of interest in high-dimensional convex geometry and local Banach space theory. In this paper, we provide a {\it dimension-independent} bound on the cotype of the corresponding normed space $({\mathbb R}^n,\|\cdot\|_{P_{N,n}})$, generated by $P_{N,n}$. Let $K'\geq K>1$, and assume that $K'\geq \frac{N}{n}\geq K$. We show that with probability $1-o(1)$, for any $k\geq 1$, and any collection $y_1,\dots,y_k$ of vectors in ${\mathbb R}^n$, $$ {\mathbb E}_σ\,\Big\|\sum_{i=1}^k σ_i y_i\Big\|_{P_{N,n}}^q \geq \frac{1}{C_q^q}\sum_{i=1}^k \big\|y_i\big\|_{P_{N,n}}^q, $$ where $σ=(σ_1,\dots,σ_k)$ is a vector of random signs, and where $q\in [2,\infty)$ and $C_q\in[1,\infty)$ may only depend on $K,K'$. We discuss the result in context of infinite-dimensional Banach spaces.

title: Multistage Stochastic Programming for Rare Event Risk Mitigation in Power Systems Management
generated_summary:
This paper presents a multistage stochastic programming framework for mitigating rare event risks in power systems that rely heavily on renewable energy sources, particularly wind. The main contribution is a novel scenario generation approach that biases forecasting toward low-probability, high-consequence events—such as "dunkelflaute" periods of prolonged low wind generation—to ensure robust operation of backup conventional plants that require multiple time stages to activate.

The methodology combines scenario tree-based stochastic optimization with Fleming-Viot (FV) particle systems for rare event sampling. The FV technique estimates probabilities of unlikely large negative changes in wind power by constraining particle copies of the stochastic process to explore rarely visited regions of the state space, yielding more accurate tail probability estimates than conventional Monte Carlo methods. These biased scenarios are integrated into a multistage optimization framework where chance constraints on demand satisfaction are replaced with hard constraints across all generated scenarios, producing conservative but robust solutions.

Numerical results on a five-stage optimization problem demonstrate that the FV-biased scenario approach effectively eliminates energy supply shortfall risk with only moderate increases in average operating cost compared to a benchmark strategy using unbiased scenarios. The findings validate the utility of coupling rare event simulation with stochastic programming for renewable energy integration, addressing the critical challenge of maintaining grid reliability as intermittent sources increasingly dominate the energy mix. The authors suggest extensions to longer horizons, additional generation sources, and stochastic demand modeling.
original_abstract: High intermittent renewable penetration in the energy mix presents challenges in robustness for the management of power systems' operation. If a tail realization of the distribution of weather yields a prolonged period of time during which solar irradiation and wind speed are insufficient for satisfying energy demand, then it becomes critical to ramp up the generation of conventional power plants with adequate foresight. This event trigger is costly, and inaccurate forecasting can either be wasteful or yield catastrophic undersupply. This encourages particular attention to accurate modeling of the noise and the resulting dynamics within the aforementioned scenario. In this work we present a method for rare event-aware control of power systems using multi-stage scenario-based optimization. A Fleming-Viot particle approach is used to bias the scenario generation towards rare realizations of very low wind power, in order to obtain a cost-effective control of conventional power plants that is robust under prolonged renewable energy shortfalls.

title: Approximation of invariant probability measures for super-linear stochastic functional differential equations with infinite delay
generated_summary:
This paper addresses the open problem of constructing explicit numerical schemes for approximating invariant probability measures (IPMs) of super-linear stochastic functional differential equations with infinite delay (SFDEswID). These equations arise in modeling long-memory phenomena in physics, biology, and economics, and their IPMs characterize crucial asymptotic behavior but are generally unavailable in closed form.

The authors propose an explicit truncation Euler–Maruyama (TEM) scheme based on a space-time double truncation strategy. The spatial truncation handles the superlinear growth of drift coefficients, while the temporal truncation addresses the infinite delay by storing only a bounded number of historical discrete-time nodes at each iteration, keeping storage cost independent of the simulation horizon.

The key results are threefold. First, the authors establish strong convergence of the numerical segment process to the exact solution on any finite time interval, achieving a convergence rate arbitrarily close to one-half under polynomial growth conditions. Second, they prove that the discrete-time transition semigroup generated by the TEM scheme admits a unique IPM that is exponentially ergodic in the Wasserstein distance. Third, they demonstrate convergence of the numerical IPM to the exact one and derive explicit convergence rates.

This work is significant because it resolves the previously open question of explicit ergodicity-preserving numerical approximation for superlinear SFDEswID, avoiding the computational overhead of implicit schemes that require solving nonlinear algebraic equations on infinite-dimensional function spaces at each step. Numerical experiments validate the theoretical findings.
original_abstract: This paper studies explicit numerical approximations of the invariant probability measures (IPMs) for stochastic functional differential equations (SFDEs) with infinite delay under one-sided Lipschitz condition on the drift coefficient. To date, numerical approximations of IPMs for super-linear SFDEs have been focused to finite-delay cases and implicit schemes that require additional computational effort. To overcome these constraints, we propose an explicit truncated Euler-Maruyama (TEM) scheme employing both time and space truncation for SFDEs with infinite delay, which is explicit and requires only finite historical storage. Firstly, we establish the strong convergence of the numerical segment process and determine its convergence rate over any finite time horizon. Next, we show that the numerical segment process generated by the TEM scheme admits a unique numerical IPM. Leveraging these results, we then prove that the numerical IPM converges to the exact IPM in the Wasserstein distance, with an explicitly obtained convergence rate.

title: Physics-Informed Deep Learning for Industrial Processes: Time-Discrete VPINNs for heat conduction
generated_summary:
This paper introduces a time-discrete Robust Variational Physics-Informed Neural Network (RVPINN) framework for solving parabolic partial differential equations, with particular application to industrial heat transfer processes. The main contribution lies in combining classical time discretization with a variational (weak) formulation that minimizes the residual's dual norm rather than the conventional mean-squared error, providing a theoretically grounded error estimator while accommodating solutions with lower regularity requirements.

The methodology employs a weak variational formulation akin to finite element methods, transferring derivative requirements from the solution to smooth test functions. At each time step, a neural network approximates the solution by minimizing a loss function that accurately approximates the residual's dual norm. This approach avoids the high regularity demands of standard PINNs, which struggle with sharp gradients and non-smooth solutions common in real-world applications.

The framework is validated through both a benchmark heat equation and an industrially relevant application modeling the freezing of coffee extracts. The industrial case involves temperature-dependent thermophysical properties—density, thermal conductivity, and heat capacity—across phase change temperatures, with boundary conditions derived from experimental measurements. Results demonstrate that the method accurately captures complex thermal behaviors without requiring linearization of nonlinear diffusion dynamics.

The significance of this work lies in providing a mathematically consistent, computationally stable mesh-free alternative to classical PINNs for transient diffusion processes, with demonstrated applicability to real industrial problems involving nonlinear material properties.
original_abstract: Neural networks offer powerful tools to solve partial differential equations (PDEs). We present a Variational Physics-Informed Neural Network (VPINN) designed for parabolic problems. Our approach combines a classical time discretization with a composed loss function, which minimizes the residual's dual norm at every time step. We validate the framework by modeling the freezing of coffee extracts in an industrial cylinder. The simulation accounts for temperature-dependent properties and experimental data. It successfully captures the thermal dynamics of the process.

title: Counting $P_3$-convex sets in graphs
generated_summary:
This paper investigates the problem of counting P₃-convex sets in graphs, where a subset S of vertices is P₃-convex if every vertex outside S has at most one neighbor in S. The authors address two central questions: which graphs maximize the number of P₃-convex sets, and what is the computational complexity of counting them.

For the extremal question, the authors develop a dynamic-programming approach for trees and characterize the connected n-vertex graphs that maximize the number of P₃-convex sets. They compare stars and paths, establishing structural results about extremal graphs. For computational complexity, they prove that counting P₃-convex sets is #P-complete, even when restricted to split graphs, demonstrating the inherent difficulty of the problem. As a positive result, they identify threshold graphs as a class where the counting problem admits a linear-time solution.

Given the #P-completeness result, the authors design exact exponential-time algorithms that improve upon the naive 2ⁿ enumeration approach. Their methods employ structural decomposition, propagation rules, and fast independent-set counting techniques. They also discuss refinements for specific graph classes that guarantee large independent sets, yielding better running times.

This work makes a significant contribution to the intersection of graph convexity theory and computational complexity, being among the first systematic studies of counting convex sets in graphs. The results bridge extremal combinatorics and algorithmic enumeration, providing both theoretical bounds and practical algorithmic tools.
original_abstract: We study the $P_3$-convexity, the path convexity generated by all three-vertex paths, and focus on the problem of counting the $P_3$-convex vertex sets of a graph $G$, denoted by $\noc(G)$. First, we settle the associated extremal question: we characterize the $n$-vertex graphs maximizing $\noc(G)$ among all graphs and determine the connected extremal graphs. Next, we investigate computational complexity and show that counting $P_3$-convex sets is $\#\mathsf{P}$-complete already on split graphs, even under additional structural restrictions. On the positive side, we identify two tractable subclasses, namely trees and threshold graphs, and obtain linear-time algorithms for both. Finally, we design nontrivial exact exponential-time algorithms for general graphs, combining structural decomposition, propagation rules capturing forced consequences of $P_3$-convexity, and fast counting of independent sets in auxiliary graphs. The resulting strategy becomes particularly effective on graph classes where large independent sets are guaranteed and can be found efficiently.

title: Covering complete $r$-partite hypergraphs with few monochromatic components
generated_summary:
This paper addresses a conjecture by Gyárfás and Király concerning the minimum number of monochromatic components needed to cover the vertices of edge-colored complete multipartite uniform hypergraphs. Specifically, the authors study the covering number tc(r, k), defined as the minimum integer such that any spanning k-coloring of a complete r-partite r-uniform hypergraph can be covered by that many monochromatic components.

The main contribution is the resolution of Conjecture 1.8 for the case k = r, proving that tc(r, r) = r − 1 for all r ≥ 3. This complements earlier work by Gyárfás and Király, who established the result for r = 3 and proved the general lower bound. The authors complete the proof by establishing the matching upper bound.

The methodology relies on associating each vertex with a vector encoding its monochromatic component memberships across all colors, then analyzing these vectors using Hamming distance arguments. The authors show that vertices in different parts of the hypergraph sharing the same component in some color can be leveraged to construct an efficient covering. The proof proceeds by case analysis on the structure of these component vectors.

Additionally, the paper proves that tc(2, k) = k for k ≥ 3, resolving the bipartite case, and poses the determination of tc(r, k) for general r < k as an open problem. These results connect to Ryser's conjecture on vertex covers in partite hypergraphs and Gyárfás's conjecture on monochromatic covers of complete graphs, contributing to a rich line of research in combinatorial covering problems.
original_abstract: An edge-coloring of a hypergraph is {\em spanning} if every vertex sees every color used in the coloring. In this paper, we prove that for $k \geq 2r \geq 6$, in any spanning $k$-coloring of the edges of a complete $r$-partite $r$-uniform hypergraph $H$, the vertices of $H$ can be covered by a set of at most $k-r+1$ monochromatic connected components. This proves a conjecture of Gyárfás and Király which is related to a special case of Ryser's conjecture. We also prove that for $k \in \{2,3\}$, every spanning $k$-edge-coloring of a complete bipartite graph admits a covering of its vertices using at most $k$ monochromatic components.

title: The Asymptotic Behaviour of Oldroyd-B Fluids is Almost Newtonian
generated_summary:
This paper investigates the long-time decay behavior of solutions to the incompressible Oldroyd-B equations in ℝⁿ, which model viscoelastic fluids. The central contribution is the surprising discovery that the asymptotic behavior of Oldroyd-B fluids is "almost Newtonian" — the elastic component of the stress tensor decays strictly faster than both the full stress tensor and its Newtonian part, implying that the viscoelastic stress asymptotically aligns with the Newtonian deformation tensor.

The methodology relies on the concept of decay character of initial data, a quantity that captures low-frequency behavior and enables sharp decay estimates for dissipative systems. The authors analyze both the corotational case (with arbitrarily large initial data and weak solutions) and the general case (with small data and strong solutions), establishing upper bounds for velocity and stress tensor decay rates that improve upon previous results. Crucially, they demonstrate that the elastic part of the stress tensor decays at a faster rate than the full stress tensor and the deformation tensor. They further establish matching lower bounds for certain classes of initial data, confirming that these decay rates are sharp and that the faster decay of the elastic component is genuine rather than an artifact of loose upper bounds.

These results have significant implications for understanding viscoelastic fluid dynamics, demonstrating that viscoelastic effects become negligible at large times and the fluid behavior converges toward Newtonian dynamics. This parallels similar asymptotic alignment phenomena observed in micropolar fluids.
original_abstract: Consider a viscoelastic fluid of Oldroyd-B type. It is shown that its stress tensor $τ$ and its Newtonian deformation tensor $D(u)$ decay at the same rate, while the elastic part $\varepsilon=τ-2ωD(u)$ decays faster. As a consequence, the stress tensor of a viscoelastic fluid exhibits an almost Newtonian behaviour for large times.

title: On regulated partitions
generated_summary:
This paper investigates regulated partitions in the context of Borel combinatorics of countable abelian group actions, revealing a fundamental dimension-dependent dichotomy. A regulated partition of ℝⁿ is obtained by replacing elements of a rectangular partition of ℤⁿ with unit cubes, creating a division of ℝⁿ into rectangles with disjoint interiors. The regulation number of a point counts how many regions meet at that point, with the minimum possible value being 2ⁿ, defining "minimal" regulated partitions.

The main contribution is a striking contrast between dimensions: for free Borel actions of ℤ on a Polish space, Borel minimal regulated partitions always exist, whereas for ℤⁿ with n ≥ 2, no Borel nondegenerate minimal regulated partition exists. This provides another instance where Borel combinatorics diverges from classical combinatorics, as minimal regulated partitions of ℤⁿ exist in the purely combinatorial setting for all dimensions. The authors introduce Borel and continuous regulation numbers and establish bounds: for n = 2, the Borel regulation number equals 5, while for general n ≥ 2 it lies between 2ⁿ + 1 and roughly 3ⁿ.

The methodology combines combinatorial analysis of minimal regulated partitions with forcing arguments from set theory. The authors prove both a finitary obstruction result for minimal locally regulated partitions in dimensions n ≥ 3 and lift it to the Borel setting using two distinct forcing constructions.

These results have implications for Borel marker constructions used in hyperfiniteness proofs and provide insight into topological regularity properties of partitions arising from abelian group actions.
original_abstract: This paper considers the combinatorics of continuous and Borel rectangular partitions of free actions of $\mathbb{Z}^n$ on $0$-dimensional Polish spaces, specifically the free part $F(2^{\mathbb{Z}^n})$ of the shift action of $\mathbb{Z}^n$ on the space $2^{\mathbb{Z}^n}$. This is done through the study of a corresponding notion of regulated partitions of $\mathbb{R}^n$. The main concepts studied are the continuous and Borel {\em regulation} numbers of the partition. This is defined as the maximum number of rectangles in the corresponding regulated partition that can intersect in a point. The continuous and Borel regulation numbers $γ_c$, $γ_B$ are the minimum possible values of these numbers as we range over continuous (respectively Borel) rectangular partitions of $F(2^{\mathbb{Z}^n})$. It is shown that for $n=2$ that $γ_c=γ_B=3$, and for $n \geq 3$ that $n+2\leq γ_B \leq γ_c \leq 3\cdot 2^{n-2}$. For $n=3$ we improve this to $γ_c=γ_B=5$. This shows a striking difference between the Borel combinatorics of dimension $n=2$ and dimensions $n>2$.

original_abstract: In this study, we focus on a generalized nonparametric scalar-on-function regression model for heterogeneously distributed and strongly mixing data. We provide almost complete convergence rates for the local linear estimator of the regression function. We show that, under our conditions, the pointwise and uniform convergence rates are the same on a compact set. On the other hand, when the data is dependent, it is proved that the convergence rate can be slower than those obtained for independent data. A simulation study shows the good performance and finite sample properties of the functional local linear estimator (FLL) in comparison to the local constant estimator (FLC). In addition, a one step ahead energy consumption forecasting exercise illustrates that the forecasts of the FLL estimator are significantly more accurate than those of the FLC.

title: The augmented van Trees inequality

This paper develops an augmented van Trees inequality that improves upon the classical van Trees inequality, a fundamental tool for deriving Bayesian and minimax risk lower bounds in statistics. The methodology is grounded in extending the standard information-theoretic proof framework while accommodating broader prior classes and the additional augmentation term.

The augmented inequality is applied to pointwise Hölder function estimation, where it yields near-sharp minimax lower bounds with improved constants, and exact constants in high-dimensional regimes. The authors further demonstrate the flexibility of their augmentation scheme by extending it to the generalized van Trees inequality, accommodating loss functions beyond mean squared error and estimation in irregular models.

The significance of this work lies in providing a remarkably simple, off-the-shelf methodology for deriving minimax lower bounds that achieves constants competitive with or better than those obtained through the substantially more complex convergence of experiments theory, making it a valuable tool for nonparametric statistics.
original_abstract: We introduce an augmented form of the van Trees inequality, that yields uniformly tighter lower bounds on the minimax squared Bayes risk of estimators compared with the classical van Trees inequality. Our augmented inequality also accommodates prior distributions whose densities need not vanish at the boundaries of their supports. We demonstrate how this refinement can be utilised for elementary proofs of a number of minimax lower bounds for nonparametric estimands, that also often attain sharper constants than those obtained by the alternative Le Cam convergence of experiments theory and the classical van Trees inequality, and in some cases obtain exact constants. As an example, our augmented van Trees inequality can be used to obtain the asymptotic minimax pointwise mean squared error when estimating the regression function in the model with normal errors: when the regression function is univariate and differentiable with Lipschitz derivative we obtain this quantity up to a constant factor of $1.37$; and in the high dimensional regime with a Hölder smooth regression function of smoothness $β\in(0,2]$ we obtain exact constants. Both these results do not follow from an application of the classical van Trees inequality. The flexibility of our augmented van Trees inequality accommodates lower bounds for models beyond Gaussianity, loss functions beyond the squared error loss, and we are also able to incorporate this augmentation into generalised versions of the van Trees inequality for irregular models.
